title: [TRTLLM-16304][feat] In-tree implementation of staircase
body:
## What this is

Staircase is an experiment in how modeling code is organized, not a new feature.

Where the built-in zoo has one class serving a whole model family across every
GPU generation and parallel topology, this has one self-contained forward per
(checkpoint, GPU architecture, parallel topology) triple: flat and readable end
to end, assembled only from a catalog of op wrappers, sharing nothing with its
siblings, and trusted through accuracy gates rather than through shared
abstractions.

It lives under `tensorrt_llm/_torch/_experimental/modeling_v2/` and stays off
unless `TRTLLM_MODELING_V2` says otherwise, so nothing changes for anyone who
does not opt in. Whether this is a better way to organize modeling code is the
question the experiment exists to answer.

---

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Adds in-tree Staircase routing with `off`, `auto`, and `require` modes controlled by `TRTLLM_STAIRCASE`.
- Adds SM103 targets for GPT-OSS 120B TP1 and DeepSeek-R1-0528 NVFP4 DEP4.
- Adds target-specific modeling, weight loading, YAML configurations, operator wrappers, and catalog contracts.
- Adds extensive operator documentation and packaging entries.
- Main risks are CUDA-only execution, strict checkpoint and topology matching, custom-operator availability, and complex weight relayout and quantization paths.
- Verify that `AutoModelForCausalLM` preserves existing behavior when routing is disabled or unmatched.
- Verify that `require` fails with actionable diagnostics and that lazy target imports do not create import-time regressions.
- Review memory settings, MTP configurations, and `TRTLLM_CAN_USE_DEEP_EP=0` requirements for consistency across launch environments.

## QA Engineer Review

- Adds unit coverage for activation, normalization, attention, GEMM, MoE, quantization, communication, routing, and target-artifact contracts.
- Adds multi-rank CUDA/MPI tests for `allgather` and `reducescatter`, including CUDA Graph, stream, validation, call-order, and wedge behavior.
- Adds integration accuracy tests for GPT-OSS 120B and DeepSeek-R1, including identity, MTP3 acceptance, GSM8K accuracy, and default routing behavior.
- Adds CI test-list entries in `l0_gb300.yml` and `l0_gb300_multi_gpus.yml` for operator, collective, accuracy, and default-behavior coverage.
- Coverage is **sufficient** for the documented CUDA and SM103 scope, but requires follow-up on unsupported architectures, non-CUDA environments, package-data installation, and full checkpoint loading.

### Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/models/modeling_auto.py`: Verify disabled, automatic, required, matched, and unmatched Staircase resolution paths.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/staircase/_router_index.py`, `__init__.py`, `explain.py`, and routing modules: Verify environment parsing, diagnostics, lazy imports, target identity, and unsupported-topology behavior.
- Staircase catalog Python files: Verify wrapper signatures, tensor validation, custom-op registration, mutation contracts, dtype behavior, and unsupported-input errors.
- Staircase catalog Markdown and `index.yaml` files: Verify documented signatures, certified configurations, limits, and implementation paths match the wrappers and tests.
- Staircase target `modeling.py` and `weights.py` files: Verify model construction, operator availability checks, weight coverage, tensor layouts, dtype handling, and post-load views against real checkpoints.
- Target YAML files: Verify topology, MTP settings, memory limits, environment requirements, and launch-time defaults.
- `setup.py`: Verify all Staircase Markdown and YAML files are included in source and wheel distributions.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/staircase/**`: Covers operator contracts, numerical behavior, edge cases, validation, routing, and artifact consistency. These tests are listed through the Staircase entries in `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_gb300.yml` where applicable.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/staircase/comm/**`: Covers launcher-driven four-rank collective behavior. The matrix entry points are listed in `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_gb300_multi_gpus.yml`.
- `tests/integration/defs/accuracy/test_staircase.py`: Covers GPT-OSS and DeepSeek accuracy, identity, MTP acceptance, and default routing. Its acceptance tests are listed in `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_gb300_multi_gpus.yml`.
- `tests/integration/defs/accuracy/references/*.yaml`: Provides accuracy and acceptance-length thresholds used by the integration tests. Verify reference provenance and threshold updates before changing certified results.
- `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_gb300.yml`: Adds single-GPU Staircase operator and model coverage.
- `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_gb300_multi_gpus.yml`: Adds ordered collective coverage and DeepSeek accuracy acceptance coverage.

title: [None][feat] Add GLM-5.3-Flash (glm5_next) support
body:
## Description

Adds GLM-5.3-Flash (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, architecture `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) to the TensorRT-LLM PyTorch backend using the official FP8 checkpoint.

Implements the GLM-5.3-Flash text decoder, native MTP, and vision tower using shared TensorRT-LLM modules. The decoder combines KDA linear attention, sparse MLA with a pool-based indexer, mHC, and MoE.

Shared KDA changes add low-rank output gates, support for 64 attention heads, and FP32 gate parameters required by GLM-5.3-Flash, while preserving the existing full-rank gate path.

**Supported features:** TP4/EP4, CUDA graphs, overlap scheduling, chunked prefill, MTP, attention DP (including MTP), FP8 KV cache, prefix reuse, image/video inputs, and text PD disaggregation with and without MTP. Validated on B200.

**Documentation:** See the deployment guide at `docs/source/deployment-guide/deployment-guide-for-glm-5.3-flash-on-trtllm.md` (serving configs, benchmarks, performance curves, and the required GLM-specific Transformers revision). Shared requirements are unchanged.

## Test Coverage

### Correctness and accuracy

- Full GSM8K comparisons against HF match within **0.08 percentage points**, with and without MTP3, under the matched thinking-mode protocol: 1,319 questions, greedy decoding, and a 4,096-token output budget.
- Separate full GSM8K regression runs using the repository harness pass for attention DP + MTP3, TP4/EP4 + FP8 KV, and attention DP + MTP3 + FP8 KV. Scores are **93.37%, 93.29%, and 93.86%**, respectively. These use the 5-shot raw-completion protocol with a 256-token output budget and are not directly comparable to the HF thinking-mode scores above.
- Native HF image/video feature parity tests pass with the required Transformers revision. Full-model validation also covers MMMU, video serving, snapshot-based prefix reuse, chunked prefill, runtime behavior, and NIXL disaggregated serving.
- Focused unit coverage checks checkpoint routing, layer masks, FP32 gate sharding, encoder-only construction, low-rank KDA projections, sparse-cache layout and dispatch, FP8 cache storage and graph replay, mixed attention-DP/MTP batches, and large KDA state offsets.

Existing unit-test stages are reused. Full-model coverage adds one TP4/EP4 MTP3 GSM8K case to the existing four-GPU GB300 pre-merge stage, with CUDA graphs, overlap scheduling, and chunked prefill enabled. Broader feature coverage is registered in post-merge and QA; no new Jenkins stages are introduced.

Local resource reference: the MTP3 GSM8K test body took approximately 7.3 minutes on 4×B200, with 8.3 minutes total launcher wall time.

### Performance

Measured on **4×B200**, with FP8 weights and BF16 KV cache, using `benchmark_serving`: 1,024 input / 1,024 output tokens, random token IDs, seed 0, greedy decoding, `ignore_eos`, and natural MTP acceptance. Each run sends `5 × concurrency` requests; plotted points aggregate matching repeated runs.

| Configuration | C=1 mean TPOT | C=128 aggregate output throughput |
|---|---:|---:|
| TP4 / EP4 | 6.52 ms | 6,032 tok/s |
| TP4 / EP4 + MTP3 | 2.69 ms | 6,287 tok/s |
| Attention DP4 / EP4 | 9.95 ms | 5,924 tok/s |
| Attention DP4 / EP4 + MTP3 | 4.18 ms | 6,270 tok/s |

MTP3 improves TP4/EP4 single-user decode speed by approximately **2.42×** on this synthetic workload. Throughput is summed across four GPUs. These measurements cover the tested concurrency range and do not establish peak throughput or maximum-context performance.

## PR Checklist

title: [None][infra] Add PrimTS vendor promotion maintainer tool
body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

The change adds a configurable vendor-promotion toolkit with metadata validation, commit attribution, lock-only promotion, and local monitoring. Promotion defaults to dry-run; remote publication requires explicit options. Recovery checks Git and GitHub artifacts and treats the SQLite cache as disposable.

The tooling does not re-vendor source files or change runtime kernels, vendor pins, compatibility patches, or dependencies. The old vendor-source and PrimTS-specific entry points are not retained, so callers must migrate to the generic commands and provide explicit vendor and repository configuration.

## QA Engineer Review

- `tests/unittest/others/test_maintain_prims_ts.py` adds promotion and recovery cases, including dry-run behavior, publication, auto-merge, validation failures, interruptions, and cache loss.
- `tests/unittest/others/test_vendor_bot.py` adds metadata and attribution, feedback, discovery, publication, workdir safety, recovery, and daemon lifecycle cases.
- `tests/unittest/others/test_vendor_sources.py` changes the test loader to use `scripts/vendor/manage.py`.
- The changed tests are unit tests. No entries for these tests appear in the `test-db/` or `qa/` integration lists.
- The PR objective reports 190 hermetic CPU-only tests passed and five live GitHub metadata-validation cases passed. It also reports that post-merge promotion and some review or dismissal paths were not validated live.
- **Coverage verdict: needs follow-up.** The reported live testing did not cover all promotion and review paths.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `scripts/vendor/manage.py`: The vendor-management entry point is now the supported interface. Verify documented commands use the new path and that repository-relative defaults resolve correctly.
- `scripts/vendor/metadata.py`: Adds metadata parsing, validation, and upstream commit attribution. Verify malformed, ambiguous, and unpaired metadata cases.
- `scripts/vendor/promote.py`: Adds dry-run and publishing workflows for lock-only promotion and follow-up PRs. Verify recovery, branch and repository validation, and explicit publication behavior.
- `scripts/vendor/bot.py`: Adds monitoring, feedback, publication, and recovery behavior. Verify dry-run defaults, workdir safety, polling, and operation after cache loss.
- `scripts/vendor/README.md`: Documents setup, operation, recovery, and command options. Verify documented defaults and flags match the CLI.
- `AGENTS.md`: Adds operator and contributor guidance. Verify its publishing, provenance, and recovery instructions stay consistent with the tooling.
- `3rdparty/vendor-sources.md`: Replaces documented legacy commands with `scripts/vendor/manage.py` and links the toolkit guide. Verify all examples use supported commands.
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml`: Runs the vendor check through `scripts/vendor/manage.py`. Verify the hook still checks vendor state.
- `.github/CODEOWNERS`: Moves ownership from the old script to `/scripts/vendor/`. Verify the new directory receives the intended review owners.
- `tests/unittest/others/test_maintain_prims_ts.py`: Covers promotion, safety checks, and recovery paths. It is not listed in the integration test lists.
- `tests/unittest/others/test_vendor_bot.py`: Covers metadata, monitor behavior, and recovery paths. It is not listed in the integration test lists.
- `tests/unittest/others/test_vendor_sources.py`: Updates tests to load the new management entry point. It is not listed in the integration test lists.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Add a reusable vendor-source toolkit and a local promotion bot. This extends the
original PrimTS maintainer command to vendor entries in
`3rdparty/vendor_sources.lock.yaml`, with operator-supplied repositories,
branches, authentication, and runtime paths rather than embedded personal
configuration.

The source-update PR reviews vendored code changes. After it merges, promotion
fast-forwards the configured canonical source branch to the exact reviewed SHA
and creates a separate lock-only PR restoring the canonical URL/branch. That
follow-up preserves the source SHA, selected files, compatibility patch, and
digests; it does not re-vendor code.

### Tool layout

| Entry point | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/vendor/manage.py` | Existing vendor create, inspect, sync, export, patch, pin, and verification operations |
| `scripts/vendor/promote.py promote` | Generic, restartable maintainer promotion and lock-only follow-up PR |
| `scripts/vendor/bot.py` | Local PR monitoring, contributor-metadata validation, automatic attribution, and promotion |
| `scripts/vendor/metadata.py` | Strict marked-block parsing and conservative upstream commit matching |
| `scripts/vendor/README.md` | Operator setup, contributor contract, workflow, usage, and safety boundaries |

`scripts/vendor_sources.py` and `scripts/maintain_prims_ts.py` are removed; use the
entry points under `scripts/vendor/` directly. No backward compatibility is
promised for those paths, PrimTS-specific CLI aliases, or legacy branch naming.
Use `--source-pr` and `--source-repo` and supply the vendor/repository configuration
explicitly. Historical `PRIMTS PROMOTION V1` provenance records remain readable;
new records use `VENDOR PROMOTION V1`.

### Local operation and authentication

- Any operator with the necessary repository permissions can use their own
  approved GitHub CLI/Git authentication. No GitHub App, webhook service, or
  systemd configuration is required.
- Support foreground monitoring, a single `--once` pass, and detached
  `--daemon` mode, plus `status` and graceful `stop` commands. A detached daemon
  does not automatically restart after a crash or reboot.
- `--workdir` selects private SQLite state, logs, source caches, process locks,
  and isolated promotion worktrees. Authentication is inherited, not stored in
  that state or committed to the repository.
- Dry-run is the default. `--publish` explicitly permits feedback, reviews,
  pushes, promotion PR creation, CI-skip requests, and auto-merge. Publishing
  through the bot always enables squash auto-merge with the provenance message.
- One process monitors one vendor. Workdir locking prevents duplicate local
  processes, while persistent state supports restart and retry reconciliation.

### Contributor metadata and author-owned ambiguity resolution

Authors provide a marked YAML block listing all upstream PRs; a complete manual
commit map is not required:

````markdown
<!-- vendor-promotion:start -->
```yaml
schema_version: 1
vendors:
  example-library:
    upstream_prs:
      - https://github.com/UPSTREAM/library/pull/123
```
<!-- vendor-promotion:end -->
````

The matcher compares immutable commit identity, whitespace/context-preserving
patches, and whole-series aggregate changes. It does not infer equivalence from
titles, cherry-pick trailers, or fuzzy similarity.

Missing or malformed metadata produces an updatable, actionable comment and an
eligible metadata-only `REQUEST_CHANGES` review. Ambiguities are reported to the
**PR author**, who can correct the upstream list, rebase/fix the pin, or provide
a targeted resolution with a reason. Author assertions are recorded as
`retain-until-verified`; updates without a paired PR require an explicit
`unpaired_reason`. Successful metadata validation never submits a code-review
approval. The bot dismisses only its own marked metadata reviews when allowed,
and reports when an authorized human must dismiss them instead.

## Maintenance workflow

The diagram below matches `scripts/vendor/README.md`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    source[Source-update PR changes a vendor pin] --> metadata[Author lists upstream PRs in description]
    metadata --> match[Bot validates metadata and matches immutable commits]
    match -->|missing or ambiguous| feedback[Request changes with author-facing instructions]
    feedback -->|author corrects block, pin, or targeted resolution| metadata
    match -->|valid and source PR merged| verify[Verify ancestry, current lock, and materialization]
    verify --> ff[Fast-forward configured canonical source branch]
    ff --> promotion[Create or reuse URL/branch-only promotion PR]
    promotion --> ci[Request CI skip and enable squash auto-merge]
    ci -->|required checks and owner reviews| merged[Verify final lock and squash provenance]
    merged --> rebase[Other source-update authors rebase onto the canonical pin]
```

Provenance is stored in the DCO-signed promotion commit and final squash message,
not another tracking file. Promotion is restartable across interrupted
worktree/commit/push/PR creation and avoids duplicate PRs and CI comments on
sequential retries. Upstream attribution is provenance, not automatic permission
to drop changes during a future refresh.

## Usage

Replace the example vendor and repository values with the intended configuration.
Start with a read-only pass:

```bash
python scripts/vendor/bot.py run \
  --vendor example-library \
  --upstream-repo UPSTREAM/library \
  --canonical-repo MAINTAINER/library \
  --canonical-branch consumer-dev \
  --fork YOUR_ACCOUNT/TensorRT-LLM \
  --workdir /path/to/private/vendor-bot-state \
  --once
```

Replace `--once` with `--daemon --publish` to detach and enable remote writes.
`--daemon` without `--publish` remains a dry run. No daemon is launched by this PR.

Manual promotion uses the same engine:

```bash
python scripts/vendor/promote.py promote \
  --vendor example-library \
  --source-pr 123 \
  --upstream-repo UPSTREAM/library \
  --canonical-repo MAINTAINER/library \
  --canonical-branch consumer-dev \
  --fork YOUR_ACCOUNT/TensorRT-LLM \
  --from-pr-description \
  --publish --auto-merge
```

Explicit `--upstream-pr` with `--auto-match`, manual `--map-upstream` assignments,
and `--unpaired-reason` remain available. Optional `--wait` verifies the final
merge. Consumer/base/upstream branches are configurable.

## Safety and scope

- Validate immutable source selection, expected canonical target, linear
  fast-forward ancestry, current consumer pin, source materialization, and the
  complete lock-only diff. Use non-force pushes and preserve completed writes
  for recovery rather than attempting destructive rollback.
- Recheck mutable PR metadata before feedback/publication. Preserve manual code
  reviews and use comment-only feedback on the operator's own PRs.
- Run one publishing operator per consumer/vendor/canonical branch. Local
  process locking is not distributed locking. Finish one promotion before
  merging the next update for that vendor.
- Existing GitHub permissions, required checks, owner reviews, and CI-bot
  authorization still apply. Merge queues are unsupported because the final
  squash message must preserve provenance.
- Promotion/monitoring currently support GitHub.com and canonical branch pins.
  Periodic upstream refresh/rebase and tag promotion are not implemented here.
- `/bot skip --comment "skip CI since no code change"` applies only to verified
  generated **lock-only promotion PRs**. This tooling PR adds Python code and
  must use normal CI; it must not take the promotion CI-skip path.

This PR changes tools, tests, documentation, the vendoring pre-commit entry point,
and CODEOWNERS coverage for `scripts/vendor/`. It does **not** change runtime
kernels, vendor pins, vendored source files, compatibility patches, or dependencies.

## Test Coverage

- **190 hermetic CPU-only tests passed** across vendoring, promotion, and bot
  suites, using temporary Git repositories and fake GitHub responses. This
  includes a real detached-process launch/status/stop smoke test with a fake
  `gh`; no GPU, credentials, or network are required for the suite.
- Coverage includes paired/unpaired provenance, automatic matching and ambiguity,
  whitespace/CRLF and function-context distinctions, malformed YAML/locks,
  author correction, review safety, private workdirs and process locking,
  non-`main` branches, publication retries, CI-comment deduplication, and final
  squash-message verification.
- Rebased onto `main` at `3cfcb0d9622e2ef7a926436dc174c96ebc9367af`.
  The sole conflict was the move of `scripts/vendor_sources.py`: the updated

## Description

Follow-up to #18933, which introduced a separate encoder execution path without a shared runner abstraction. This PR establishes common contracts for the encoder and existing decoder paths, laying the groundwork for the decoder runner refactor.

title: [None][perf] MXFP8 locality-domain split: one parent reset for both shards, static planner decision
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #19469 (merged as f94eeb3738). Three commits:

1. **One parent reset for both locality-domain shards** (below).
2. **Static planner decision, shards as the only weight copy** (see below).
3. **[chore] Drop the cached-FC2 tactic from the split** so its tactic space equals the full-GPU op's and cannot be misled by warm profiling (concurrent partition tuning cannot use the cold-L2 mode). No measurable performance change (table at the end).

 The MXFP8 locality-domain split of the fused FC12 MoE launched each shard through the full fused op, so a split call paid two workspace resets, a standalone output memset (with its aux-stream event pair) and, because raw activations could not be handed to two concurrent shards, a standalone `mxfp8_quantize` launch. Those launches cost more than the split's kernel-level locality gain, which is why `enable_locality_domains` was neutral to slightly negative per MoE call.

This PR runs **one parent reset for both shards** on the caller's stream before the fork:

- `fused_fc12_workspace.py`: the reset kernel takes an optional second workspace (ready flags + two counters) and clears both partitions in one launch.
- `cute_dsl_custom_ops.py`: `Sm107Mxfp8FusedFc12MoeRunner` gains `skip_reset` (shard launches do no reset and require E4M3 input), class-level accessors for the cached sync workspace and input-quant scratch, and `launch_locality_domain_parent_reset` (both workspaces, whole-output clear under `zero_output`, BF16/FP16 -> MXFP8 quantization into the shared scratch, PDL against the preceding kernel). The composite op `cute_dsl_mxfp8_fused_fc12_moe_locality_domain_inplace_rubin` gains `zero_output`, registers the parent reset as the concurrent tuning runner's prologue and launches the skip-reset runner directly per partition (no nested custom op).
- `locality_domain/autotune.py`: `LocalityDomainConcurrentTunableRunner` / `tune_locality_domain_concurrent` accept an optional `prologue_fn` that runs before the fork on every forward, profiling included.
- `fused_moe_cute_dsl.py`: raw activations reach the split like the full-GPU op (the quant fusion no longer depends on the recorded per-token decision; `_mxfp8_full_gpu_path_selected` is removed) and the split path passes `zero_output` under the same dense-case rule instead of launching the separate memset.

Per split call: routing, one parent reset, two shard GEMMs (4 launches) instead of routing, quantize, memset, two resets, two shard GEMMs (6 launches + event pair). Locality domains stay **off by default**.

## Verification (Rubin SM107, wheel built from feat/rl_rc, python overlaid)

- `test_cute_dsl_moe.py -k locality_domain_op_matches_full_gpu`: 2 passed. Adds a split call with raw BF16 input and a dirty (3.0-filled) output under `zero_output`; it matches the E4M3 split and the full-GPU op within the split tolerance. (The two shards scatter-add concurrently with BF16 atomics, so runs are not bitwise identical to each other; the test compares within tolerance.)
- CPU: composite ownership / fake signature / concurrent tunable runner / input-quant and admission rules: 18 passed. `test_fc12_input_quant.py`: 39 passed. `test_locality_domain_planner.py`: 55 passed, 7 skipped. `test_moe_backend.py -k cutedsl_mxfp8_fused_fc12`: 3 passed.

## Performance (same wheel, module-level `quantize_input` + `run_moe` per call, Rubin, HBM 4752 MHz)

CUDA-graph replays, 4 module copies rotated so weights are cold in L2, Qwen3.5-397B geometry (512 experts, top-k 10, hidden 4096, intermediate 1024), power-law routing (alpha 0.8), worst rank per token count. Microseconds; "off" = locality domains disabled (unchanged by this PR), "on" = enabled with this PR.

| layout | tokens/rank | off | on (before) | on (this PR) | vs off |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TEP8 (64 local experts) | 4 | 17.99 | 19.60 | 17.65 | -2% |
| | 8 | 22.21 | 22.32 | 20.65 | -7% |
| | 16 | 28.72 | 27.62 | 25.72 | -10% |
| | 32 | 34.19 | 36.19 | 28.73 | -16% |
| | 64 | 45.85 | 46.31 | 37.74 | -18% |
| | 128 | 58.20 | 60.81 | 49.73 | -15% |
| | 256 | 66.44 | 70.09 | 55.36 | -17% |
| DEP4 (128 local experts) | 8 | 52.12 | 53.33 | 43.51 | -17% |
| | 16 | 74.54 | 73.05 | 60.32 | -19% |
| | 32 | 100.60 | 98.24 | 81.13 | -19% |
| DEP16 (32 local experts) | 4 | 25.95 | 30.50 | 24.35 | -6% |
| | 16 | 37.76 | 41.54 | 34.74 | -8% |
| | 32 | 43.01 | 46.32 | 40.16 | -7% |

1-2 tokens are within noise (the selector keeps the full-GPU op there). nsys at 16 tokens, forced split: routing 0-3.2 us, parent reset 2.9-4.3 us (overlapping routing under PDL), shard GEMMs 3.8-23.9 / 4.3-25.1 us on the two partition streams; 4 kernels per call. The shard GEMMs also got faster (22.7 -> 20.1 us) without the quantize launch competing for the GPU.

## Commit 2: static planner decision (as for NVFP4 / BF16), shards are the only copy

The MXFP8 split was a per-shape runtime choice: the autotuner profiled the full-GPU op and the split side by side, a per-token decision picked one (inside a 2048-row / 4096-route admission rule), and to keep that option open the module kept **both** the full expert weights and the shards resident, doubling the MoE weight memory whenever the flag was on. This commit follows the NVFP4 and BF16 paths: with `enable_locality_domains` the planner decides once, every shape of the layer runs the split (its tile / weight-streaming tactics stay autotuned), and `post_load_weights` releases the full parameters after sharding. The selector, its decision cache and the admission rule are removed. A refit after the release (RLHF) re-creates the full parameters transiently in `load_weights`; `post_load_weights` re-shards and releases them again.

**Bug fix (latent in #19469 and in the tekit MR):** the shard block scales were unswizzled and re-swizzled with the module's NVFP4 scale-vector size (16) instead of the MXFP8 block size (32), so the split computed with wrong scales whenever it ran. The op-level test did not catch it because it slices shards with its own helper; the flag is off by default, so the merged default path is unaffected.

**New test** `test_moe_module_mxfp8_locality_domain_static_split_rubin` (2 passed on Rubin): shards an MXFP8 layer, checks the full parameters and quant scales are released, checks the shards concatenate to exactly the base weights, compares the split against the full-GPU module at 16 and 4096 rows (0.5% RMS relative, cosine 0.99999: the shards' extra BF16 rounding of the partial FC2 sums at ~1e5 output magnitude; the MXFP8 quantization itself sits at 2.7% RMS from exact math) and repeats after a refit reload. All other sections re-pass (split op 2, CPU rules 18, kernel 39, planner 55, backend A/B 3).

**Performance, same node and wheel** (Rubin, module-level `quantize_input` + `run_moe` per call, cold weights, HBM 4752 MHz, Qwen3.5-397B geometry, power-law routing, worst rank, us):

| layout | tokens/rank | off | on (static split) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TEP8 | 1 / 2 | 14.80 / 15.18 | 14.30 / 14.70 | -3% |
| | 4 / 8 | 17.53 / 20.51 | 20.11 / 21.89 | +15% / +7% |
| | 16 / 32 | 25.12 / 30.89 | 24.88 / 29.03 | -1% / -6% |
| | 64 / 128 / 256 | 42.24 / 58.61 / 66.95 | 37.50 / 49.58 / 55.43 | -11% / -15% / -17% |
| DEP4 | 1 / 2 / 4 | 20.52 / 26.69 / 35.42 | 22.55 / 25.29 / 33.56 | +10% / -5% / -5% |
| | 8 / 16 / 32 | 53.30 / 75.31 / 101.00 | 43.19 / 61.18 / 81.17 | -19% / -19% / -20% |
| DEP16 | 1 / 2 / 4 | 17.92 / 23.37 / 25.78 | 18.45 / 23.03 / 23.77 | +3% / -1% / -8% |
| | 8 / 16 / 32 | 32.03 / 38.02 / 42.74 | 30.29 / 34.63 / 40.46 | -5% / -9% / -5% |

Without a runtime choice the split costs 7-15% at TEP8 4-8 tokens and 3-10% at 1 token/rank on DEP; it saves 5-20% everywhere else and the weight memory no longer doubles. Prefill-sized rows also run the split (about 20% slower than the full-GPU op at 16K rows/rank in isolated measurements), so enable the flag on decode (generation) engines, as for the NVFP4/BF16 splits.

## TEP8 sweep, 1 to 16384 tokens, all versions on one node

This is the authoritative TEP8 table: all arms ran back to back on one node. The earlier per-commit tables above combined an "on" arm from one job with an "off" arm from another node, and at 1-8 tokens the node-to-node and autotune variance (about 1-2 us) is as large as the effect, so their small-token rows should not be read as precise; from 16 tokens/rank up the differences dwarf the variance.

Same wheel, same node (Rubin, HBM 4752 MHz), module-level `quantize_input` + `run_moe` per call, cold weights (4 module copies), Qwen3.5-397B geometry, power-law routing, worst rank, microseconds. "off" is the full-GPU path, identical in every version. "base" is feat/rl_rc at f94eeb3738 with locality on (runtime selector, admission rule up to 2048 rows; its split ran with the wrong shard scales, which affects results but not timing). "c1" is the first commit of this PR (parent reset, selector kept), "c2" the second (static split, shards only).

| tokens | off | base on | | c1 on | | c2 on | |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 14.99 | 15.32 | +2% | 14.93 | 0% | 14.25 | -5% |
| 2 | 15.56 | 16.05 | +3% | 15.70 | +1% | 14.84 | -5% |
| 4 | 18.03 | 19.39 | +8% | 18.06 | 0% | 20.06 | +11% |
| 8 | 22.26 | 22.05 | -1% | 22.94 | +3% | 22.54 | +1% |
| 16 | 29.99 | 28.04 | -7% | 30.28 | +1% | 26.25 | -13% |
| 32 | 33.74 | 33.56 | -1% | 30.92 | -8% | 31.22 | -8% |
| 64 | 42.50 | 46.67 | +10% | 42.33 | 0% | 42.30 | 0% |
| 128 | 58.63 | 61.55 | +5% | 55.21 | -6% | 55.50 | -5% |
| 256 | 66.37 | 69.49 | +5% | 62.44 | -6% | 62.17 | -6% |
| 512 | 74.12 | 76.74 | +4% | 68.96 | -7% | 68.63 | -7% |
| 1024 | 78.62 | 82.05 | +4% | 73.30 | -7% | 72.93 | -7% |
| 2048 | 88.94 | 93.97 | +6% | 84.66 | -5% | 85.56 | -4% |
| 4096 | 112.16 | 112.02 | 0% | 112.09 | 0% | 111.22 | -1% |
| 8192 | 157.07 | 156.77 | 0% | 158.18 | +1% | 176.58 | +12% |
| 16384 | 228.69 | 228.60 | 0% | 230.09 | +1% | 281.58 | +23% |

- Before this PR the selected split was mostly a loss (4-10% slower from 64 to 2048 tokens) because of its two resets, separate quantize and separate memset; above 2048 the admission rule kept the full-GPU op.
- Commit 1 turns the selected split into a 5-8% gain from 32 through 2048 tokens with no change elsewhere.
- Commit 2 (static, one weight copy) matches or beats commit 1 wherever the split runs (-5% at 1-2 tokens, -13% at 16, -4..-8% at 32-2048) and adds the two costs of having no shape filter: +11% at 4 tokens, and the prefill penalty at 8K-16K rows/rank (+12% / +23%, the inner-channel split's tile-efficiency loss once the kernel is compute-bound). As with the NVFP4/BF16 splits, enable the flag on decode (generation) engines and leave it off on context engines.

## Same-node check of the cached-FC2 tactic removal (commit 3) and node sensitivity

Rubin, one node (a different one from the sweep above), same wheel, TEP8 worst rank, cold weights, us:

| tokens | off | split, cached-FC2 allowed | split, streaming only (commit 3) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 / 2 | 14.78 / 15.18 | 15.02 / 14.74 | 14.57 / 14.66 |
| 4 / 8 | 17.58 / 19.42 | 20.13 / 21.90 | 20.12 / 22.04 |
| 16 / 32 | 27.55 / 33.74 | 24.95 / 29.05 | 24.97 / 29.05 |
| 64 / 128 / 256 | 42.23 / 58.67 / 67.20 | 37.51 / 49.59 / 55.46 | 37.07 / 49.18 / 55.24 |
| 512 / 1024 / 2048 | 73.69 / 81.68 / 89.05 | 61.32 / 65.87 / 79.21 | 61.04 / 66.05 / 80.74 |
| 4096 / 8192 / 16384 | 116.78 / 155.95 / 226.67 | 105.95 / 186.30 / 281.00 | 106.12 / 186.74 / 281.56 |

The two split variants agree within 1-2% everywhere (3% at 1 token, within the run-to-run spread), so commit 3 is hygiene.

**How large the module-level gain is, honestly.** Across three nodes the module-level split gain at 32-256 tokens measured 4-8% (hecate0036), 9-19% (hecate0090) and 5-9% (hecate0177, rotation 8); the sign is consistent, the size is node-dependent, and 5-10% is the fair headline. An op-level measurement of the same two ops (E4M3 input supplied, op incl. its own reset, best of both routing tiles, rotation 4 or 8) shows the split only 0-2% ahead of the full-GPU op at 64-256 tokens and 7-15% behind at 4-32. The difference is which rank is called "worst": the module benchmark takes the rank with the most local routes (e.g. 59 routes over 23 experts at 32 tokens), the op-level one the slowest rank by time (43 routes over 27 experts); more rows per expert tile is where halving the inner channels helps a CTA, so the split's advantage is largest on the route-heaviest rank, which is also the rank that bounds the MoE step. Two observations from the traces at 1-16 tokens: (a) at 1-2 tokens (3-5 routes) each half-channel shard kernel is 0.5-0.8 us shorter than the full kernel because a few CTAs are limited by per-CTA weight streaming and each shard streams half the bytes; (b) at 4-8 tokens (9-17 routes) the full kernel is already close to the aggregate HBM limit, so the split cannot cut the bytes and each shard runs 1-1.5 us *longer* than the whole kernel (doubled input/metadata gathers, both shards' atomics on the same output rows, and the slower shard sets the pace), hence +13-15%. From 16 tokens per-CTA FC1 work is large enough for the half-channel split to win and the gain grows with routes. Note the split is more node-sensitive than the full-GPU op: flag-off agrees with the other node within 1-4%, while the split measured 9-19% under flag-off here against 4-8% there at the same token counts.

## Reference: kernel-level TP8 comparison (not part of this PR's change)

One GPU (Rubin, HBM 4752 MHz), TP8 / MoE-TP8 / no EP layout (512 local experts, intermediate 128 per rank), identical power-law routing and weights, E4M3 input outside the timed call, each op incl. its own reset/clear, 8 cold weight copies, us per call:

| tokens | active experts / routes | CuTe kernel at MR 10663 base | ours (feat/rl_rc + this PR) | HMMA (tekit MR 10663) | CUDA-core (fc12-mxfp8-tp8-study, requant mode) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

body:

## Dev Engineer Review

## QA Engineer Review

- Added CUDA-only precision tests for sequence lengths 4096–16384 with TF32 enabled and disabled. The tests compare cosine and sine tables with a float64 reference, use `5e-3` absolute tolerance, require a TF32-capable GPU, use integer spatial IDs, and restore the original TF32 setting.
- Added a waiver in `tests/integration/test_lists/waives.txt` for the GB300 DeepSeek V4 Pro `ctx_only` performance-sanity test.
- The changed unit test is listed in `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_b200.yml`.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/visual_gen/models/cosmos3/transformer_cosmos3.py`: Verify rotary-table outputs for large positions with TF32 enabled and disabled. Confirm video-frame quality remains stable.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_cosmos3_transformer.py`: Covers long-sequence rotary-table precision under both TF32 settings. It is listed in `tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_b200.yml`.
- `tests/integration/test_lists/waives.txt`: Adds a waiver for the GB300 DeepSeek V4 Pro `ctx_only` performance-sanity case. Verify that the waiver is scoped correctly and tracked against NVBUG 6778910.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Cosmos3 video quality degrades on Blackwell inside the NGC release images: frames past t≈40 smear and never recover (Laplacian sharpness retention 0.63 vs 0.94 on a healthy stack). Reported and confirmed by two people on GB200 during the cookbook review in NVIDIA/cosmos#310 (see https://github.com/NVIDIA/cosmos/pull/310#pullrequestreview-5270331256); the same image on B200 is degraded as well (0.72), H100/H200 are fine.

Root cause: NGC PyTorch images set `TORCH_ALLOW_TF32_CUBLAS_OVERRIDE=1`, so fp32 GEMMs run in TF32. `Qwen3VLTextRotaryEmbedding.forward` built the 3D mRoPE angle table as `inv_freq @ position_ids`, an fp32 batched matmul with inner dimension 1. On sm100 cuBLAS serves that shape with a TF32 kernel for the sequence lengths Cosmos3 produces, and TF32's 10-bit mantissa cannot represent positions above 2048. Cosmos3 positions reach ~10k (4096 text tokens, modality margin, fps-scaled vision positions), so the rotary phase of late tokens is off by up to 5 rad. Late frames carry the largest positions, hence the time-dependent smearing. On sm90 cuBLAS picks a non-TF32 kernel for that shape, and pip torch 2.13 is exact on both.

Fix: the table is an outer product, so compute it with an elementwise multiply. Same arithmetic, no GEMM, unaffected by any matmul precision setting. Output is bit-identical on stacks that were already correct (native aarch64 build and the rc27 wheel: same output sha256 before and after) and healthy inside the unchanged NGC image on GB200 (retention 0.939). No change to container environment or global torch flags.

Evidence, same GB200, same cookbook forward-dynamics request, seed 0:

| stack | sharpness retention |
|---|---|
| NGC rc26 image as shipped | 0.632 |
| image, `TORCH_ALLOW_TF32_CUBLAS_OVERRIDE=0` | 0.939 |
| image, attention pinned to flash | 0.639 (attention is not the cause) |
| image + this fix, TF32 left on | 0.939 |
| pip rc27 wheel / native head, with or without the fix | 0.939, identical bytes |

Micro-check of the K=1 fp32 matmul against fp64 inside the image: H200 0.0005, B200 5.06 rad, GB200 5.06 rad; the elementwise multiply is 4.85e-4 (the fp32 floor) everywhere.

Note for owners of other models: `tensorrt_llm/_torch/models/modeling_gemma4_vision.py` has the same `inv_freq @ position_ids` pattern. Its positions are image-patch indices and unlikely to exceed 2048, so it should not bite, but the pattern has the same TF32 exposure on Blackwell. Left out of this PR on purpose.

## Test Coverage

- New `TestRotaryTablePrecision` in `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_cosmos3_transformer.py` (already in `l0_b200.yml`): builds the rotary table at sequence lengths 4096/6240/8192/10336/16384, fractional temporal axis included, with `allow_tf32` False and True, and checks cos/sin against an fp64 reference within the fp32 floor. No checkpoint needed. Verified on GB200 inside the rc26 image: the old matmul fails the `allow_tf32=True` cases at 4096..10336 (cuBLAS picks a TF32 kernel only at some sizes; 16384 happens to be exact), the fix passes 10/10; pip torch 2.13 passes 10/10 with and without the override.
- Manual: Cosmos3-Nano forward-dynamics cookbook request on GB200 inside `nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/release:1.3.0rc26.dev202609060001` with and without the fix (table above).

title: [DIS-2903][feat] Expose scheduled batch size without iteration statistics
body:
## Description

With `enable_iter_perf_stats: false`, the existing Prometheus batch gauges lose their data source. Add `trtllm_scheduled_batch_size`, published directly by the PyTorch scheduler before forward, so prefill and decode worker batch sizes remain observable without iteration statistics or iteration logging.

Tracking: [DIS-2903](https://linear.app/nvidia/issue/DIS-2903/feature-expose-inflight-batch-size-as-metric).

- Count real context plus generation requests after resource preparation, excluding attention-DP dummies. Cover non-overlap, overlap, and pipeline execution; clear rejected batches, idle waits, and executor cleanup.
- Match the server's `model_name` and `engine_type` labels, including local-directory basenames and served-model aliases, while preserving per-rank/per-process series. Existing stats-derived metrics retain their behavior.
- Initialize the shared Prometheus directory before executor startup, preserve its owner across repeated initialization, and propagate it into MPI pools. Validate and log supplied paths, and warn when a worker cannot publish because its directory is unavailable or Prometheus was imported too early.

Enable with the existing `return_perf_metrics: true`; `enable_iter_perf_stats` and `print_iter_log` can both be false. The gauge adds no CUDA timing or iteration-stat collection. Request timing enabled by `return_perf_metrics` still applies.

The name describes a scheduled batch, matching the quantity represented by iteration stats' `numScheduledRequests`. It is not a count of all active or outstanding requests. For PP it reports the latest microbatch scheduling decision and can be zero while other microbatches remain in flight. The native endpoint collects only processes sharing its metrics directory. Multiprocess `all` mode retains PID series; a hard-killed worker can leave its last value, so deployments must use a fresh directory and must not use this gauge to infer liveness. These limitations, offline-constructor environment effects, and scrape sampling are documented in `examples/serve/README.md`.

## Test Coverage

The registered `l0_cpu.yml` metric test module now includes 36 cases covering real executor initialization, accepted/rejected batches in all three scheduler modes with iteration stats on/off, exception/normal cleanup, dummy filtering, separate workers/ranks, bounded subprocess teardown, supplied-directory validation/logging, and idle reset. A fresh interpreter drives the public `LLM` constructor with an initially unset environment variable and verifies mmap files plus a scrape at the model-build boundary. HTTP endpoint tests verify local/hub model names, served aliases, backend separation, and preservation of existing metrics.

- All 36 metric tests and both `TestHubIdRevalidation` cases passed (38 total) using the actual wheel built by [CI run #61976](https://nv/trt-llm-cicd/job/main/job/L0_MergeRequest_PR/61976/) (`1.3.0rc29`, commit `e88f6e05e4`) with the updated test files. Scheduler-loop fixtures use the real `ScheduledRequests` class.
- Verified environment restoration when `PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR` starts unset or set.
- Includes the existing test-only fix from [#19582](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/19582): current `main` removed `llm_build_stats` and `workspace` from `CachedModelLoader`, while the DFlash test fixture still passed them. This caused the two baseline CI failures; the reused fix updates the fixture without changing production behavior.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` passed. The type-check hook passed in its documented lightweight mode (17 source files; compiled TRT-LLM bindings are unavailable on this workstation).
- Based on `main` at `3cfcb0d962`; [fresh CI requested](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/19418#issuecomment-5792340427) for `0ec7ccf3cc`.

Runtime qualification: focused tests ran in the PyTorch 26.08 container with torch `2.14.0a0+4fdf77b940.nv26.8.63802676`, Prometheus client `0.26.0`, the actual CI-built wheel, and the repository's CUDA stub helper for CPU-only imports. No production source was overlaid; the only change after the wheel's commit is the DFlash test fixture. Full CI for the new test-only commit is still pending.

### Prior GPU validation (commit `4073b344c9`, before the review updates)

Two H100 PCIe 80 GB GPUs, Qwen3-0.6B, separate prefill/non-overlap and decode/overlap workers, NIXL KV transfer. Each run completed 29 requests with 2,048 input tokens and 256 output tokens, using concurrency waves `1, 4, 12, 3, 8, 1` and idle gaps. `print_iter_log` remained false throughout.

| Iteration stats | Worker | Forward batches | Batches matched to HTTP iteration stats | Prometheus HTTP samples | Observed batch sizes |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Enabled | Prefill | 19 | 19 / 19 | 2,231 | 0–2 |
| Enabled | Decode | 1,600 | 1,600 / 1,600 | 2,235 | 0–12 |
| Disabled | Prefill | 19 | No iteration-stat output | 2,425 | 0–2 |
| Disabled | Decode | 1,607 | No iteration-stat output | 2,430 | 0–12 |

**Zero mismatches:** every stats-enabled forward publication equaled `inflightBatchingStats.numScheduledRequests`, matched by iteration ID against both the raw stats object and the exported `/metrics` history. Separate HTTP scrapes checked the value visible through `/prometheus/metrics`. All 9,266 samples in stable publication windows matched exactly; the remaining 55 scrapes spanning transitions matched a published value within their HTTP request interval. Both workers returned zero during the final idle interval, before shutdown. With stats disabled, `/metrics` returned `[]` and no workload iteration-stat records were produced, while the gauge continued changing.

Validation observers only recorded actual gauge reads, publication time bounds, and independently constructed iteration stats. They did not set metric values or alter scheduling, and are excluded from this PR.

Runtime qualification: GPU runs used `nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/release:1.3.0rc27.dev202609170000` (inner wheel verified) with the original metric patch applied. Today's main requires a newer `StorageStatistics` C++ binding unavailable in that published nightly. All added metric logic was unchanged; one unchanged patch-context line was adapted for the nightly's `total_num_active_requests` parameter name. Full current-main binary validation remains for CI. These GPU runs predate the metric rename, label normalization, diagnostics, and expanded regression tests; they have not been repeated for this update.

- [x] Reviewed the repository checklist: implementation and rationale documented, CPU cases registered for CI, additive metric labeled `api-compatible`, no new dependencies or Python/configuration API fields, no ownership changes.

title: [https://nvbugs/6713426][fix] Fence DeepGEMM MegaMoE warmup launches with an EP barrier
body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

The warmup path enables an EP-group host barrier before `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` launches. The fence skips single-rank EP groups and CUDA graph capture, and it remains disabled for serving launches. Waits of at least 10 seconds generate a warning. The fence adds synchronization during warmup; review findings and test execution results were not supplied.

## QA Engineer Review

The new CPU-only tests cover barrier ordering, skipped-barrier conditions, and fence-state updates during warmup transitions. Coverage verdict: **needs follow-up** because the supplied information does not establish test execution or test-list status.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/moe/fused_moe/MOE_DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md` — Documents the warmup barrier, its scope, and the DeepGEMM barrier timeout. Verify that the documentation matches runtime behavior.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/moe/fused_moe/mega_moe/mega_moe_deepgemm.py` — Adds the host-side EP barrier before kernel launch under the specified conditions. Verify behavior for warmup, serving, graph capture, and single-rank EP.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/model_engine.py` — Connects warmup-state transitions to the fence switch. Verify that transitions enable and disable the fence as intended.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/test_mega_moe_warmup_fence.py` — Adds CPU-only checks for barrier ordering, skip conditions, and warmup-state transitions. Test-list inclusion in CI or manual-QA lists is not established by the supplied information.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

The DeepGEMM MegaMoE kernel (`fp8_fp4_mega_moe`) synchronizes the EP ranks with in-kernel barriers (`comm/barrier.cuh`) that trap after `DG_BARRIER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (60 s by default). The trap is a sticky CUDA error, so every rank that was waiting dies and the generation server goes down; what CI shows is a later `cuEventRecord` failure during KV cache teardown.

In the first warmup forwards a rank can reach its first MegaMoE launch more than a minute after its peers while it pays for one-time work. On GB300, with the CUDA driver's JIT cache on shared network storage, the driver's exclusive lock on the cache index serialized the ranks across nodes: single ranks arrived 55-73 s late and the other ranks trapped with `DeepGEMM grid sync timeout (60s)`. Moving only the JIT cache to local storage removed the trap. The fence below does not depend on what delays the rank.

**Fix**

- `mega_moe_deepgemm.py`: while the warmup launch fence is on, `run_moe` calls `dist.barrier(group=self._ep_pg)` right before `dg.fp8_fp4_mega_moe`. The NCCL barrier is ordered after the work already queued on the current stream and blocks the host, so the ranks enter the kernel together and its barrier only sees kernel-level skew; the wait is bounded by the process group timeout instead of the kernel's 60 s. It is skipped under CUDA graph capture and for `ep_size == 1`, and waits of 10 s or more are logged.
- `model_engine.py`: the `is_warmup` setter, which every warmup transition passes through and which already selects the MoE all-to-all warmup budget, switches the fence. Serving launches are not fenced, so the cost is one EP barrier per MegaMoE launch during warmup only.

## Test Coverage

- New `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/test_mega_moe_warmup_fence.py` (cpu_only; the CPU stage collects it through `unittest/_torch/moe` in `l0_cpu.yml`): the barrier runs before the kernel only while the fence is on, never during CUDA graph capture or for a single-rank EP group, and the engine's warmup transitions switch it.
- End to end on GB300 with a CI-shaped disaggregated DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4 setup (3 context servers with dep4, 1 generation server with dep32), the trigger above armed and the DeepGEMM barrier timeout at its 60 s default. The launch scripts of the two runs are identical except for the container name.
  - Without this change: ranks 55-73 s late, `DeepGEMM grid sync timeout (60s)` on the other ranks, generation server down.
  - With this change: at the first warmup launch 31 of 32 EP ranks waited at the fence for the one late rank (median 103.7 s, max 112.0 s); at the MTP layer's first launch 28 ranks waited 10-14 s; no barrier timeout on any server, and the full test (`perf/test_perf_sanity.py::test_e2e[disagg-gen_only-gb300_deepseek-v4-pro-fp4_8k1k_con180_ctx3_dep4_gen1_dep32_eplb384_mtp3_ccb-NIXL]`, including the benchmark) passed. The fence sits immediately before the launch, so these waits are what the ranks would otherwise have spent spinning in the kernel's barrier.

body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Adds multimodal admission validation through `validate_multimodal_request_data`.
- Updates executor loops to handle non-fatal `_forward_step` failures.
- Raises `RuntimeError` on the last pipeline-parallel rank when forward output is missing.
- Adds warnings when decode concurrency exceeds CUDA graph coverage.
- Review finding counts are unavailable.

## QA Engineer Review

- Adds CPU-only tests for executor failure handling, pipeline-parallel errors, multimodal validation, and CUDA graph warnings.
- Updates chunked-transfer request initialization.
- Coverage verdict: **needs follow-up** because test execution results are not supplied.
- No changed integration test-list or manual-QA list files were identified.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/models/modeling_multimodal_mixin.py`: Adds request admission validation. Verify accepted and rejected multimodal requests.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/_util.py`: Adds CUDA graph coverage warnings. Verify thresholds and suppression when graphs are disabled.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/py_executor.py`: Changes forward-failure handling and multimodal validation. Verify collectives, error paths, and pipeline-parallel behavior.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_budget_split.py`: Tests CUDA graph coverage warning cases. Test-list registration was not verified.
- `tests/unittest/executor/test_forward_error_survival.py`: Tests forward-failure survival, pipeline-parallel errors, and multimodal validation. Test-list registration was not verified.
- `tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_chunked_transfer.py`: Tests request validation after multimodal data initialization. Test-list registration was not verified.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

A non-fatal forward error is supposed to be survivable: `_forward_step` catches the exception, fails the affected requests via `_handle_errors` (which enqueues their error responses) and returns `None`. But none of the executor loops checked for that `None`, so the next statement dereferenced `batch_outputs['logits']`, crashed the event loop on every rank, and the whole engine died behind a correct-looking client error response.

This PR has two commits:

**Commit 1 — survive a failed forward step:**
- The overlap and non-overlap loops handle a `None` forward result by skipping the iteration's sampling and bookkeeping (the failed requests already got their error responses) while keeping the rank-symmetric flush collectives in place.
- The PP loop raises an explicit `RuntimeError` on the last PP rank instead of the opaque `TypeError`: inter-PP peers are inside inter-PP communication for the microbatch and cannot skip it in lockstep, so the iteration is not survivable there.
- A new `MultimodalModelMixin.validate_multimodal_request_data` hook, called from `PyExecutor._validate_request`, lets a model reject a bad multimodal payload (e.g. an image whose vision-attention segment exceeds the encoder budget) at admission time. The same condition raised inside the model forward is handled batch-wide and fails every request scheduled alongside the bad one; rejecting at admission fails only that request.

**Commit 2 — warn when admitted decode concurrency outruns CUDA graph coverage:**
The configured decode concurrency (scheduler `max_batch_size`, and any KV-capacity ceiling a cache manager reports via a worst-case per-request cost) can sit well past the range covered by captured CUDA graphs. Decode batches above that range run in eager mode, whose per-iteration latency is far higher than a graph replay, so the extra concurrency can cost throughput instead of buying it (measured: admitted ~86 vs graphs to 32 took the mean decode iteration from 65 ms to 1610 ms, ~5x output-throughput collapse). Coverage is not the largest captured size: without `cuda_graph_config.enable_padding` a decode batch replays a graph only at an exactly captured size, so the covered range is the dense `{1..n}` prefix of the capture set. Emit a one-time engine-init warning naming the remedies (raise `cuda_graph_config.max_batch_size` / `batch_sizes` with `enable_padding`, or lower `max_batch_size`). A warning rather than a refusal, because all-eager decode is a legitimate choice at low offered load; silent when CUDA graphs are disabled outright.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/executor/test_forward_error_survival.py` (CPU-only, new): the admission hook contract (default accept, override reject), the `_validate_request` call site (reject via hook, text-only skip, hook-less models), and loop-level `None` handling — the non-overlap and overlap loops complete the iteration and keep running without sampling, and the PP loop raises the explicit fatal — via stubbed executor shells driving the real loop bodies.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_budget_split.py` (CPU-only): `TestGraphCaptureConcurrencyWarning` covers the warning trigger, the no-padding dense-prefix coverage semantics, padded coverage suppressing the warning, scheduler-capped admission, and graphs-disabled silence.

title: [None][infra] Retry the mypy type-check step in the build stage
body:
## Description

The type-check step in `runLLMBuild` runs `scripts/run_mypy.sh` through a plain `sh`, with no retry. `[tool.mypy]` in `pyproject.toml` sets `install_types = true`, so before mypy checks anything it pip-installs the 27 missing stub packages from the internal PyPI mirror. 

Wrap the step in `trtllm_utils.llmExecStepWithRetry` with `shortCommondRunTimeMax: 240`, so a failure within 240s is always retried (a longer failure still goes through the usual failure-signature matching). A genuine type error surfaces well inside that window as well, but the check takes a couple of minutes at most, so the extra attempts are cheap next to failing a whole build on a mirror hiccup.

title: [None][fix] Scope KVCM warmup capacity constraints to DeepSeek V4
body:
## Description

DeepSeek V4's maximum-sequence-length warmup constraint was moved into generic KVCM V2 in #16545. For ordinary attention models, that hard floor can enlarge the temporary KV pool beyond its estimated GPU budget, causing OOM during cache creation or encoder profiling.

Restore the longest-decode-plus-short-requests constraint to `DeepseekV4CacheManager`. Keep the general context/chunked-prefill constraint in generic V2: it covers the configured per-iteration token budget. Preserve V4's draft/extra reservations, explicit pool-ratio opt-out, and generic average-length pool preferences.

Also correct generation dummy allocation at the source. `token_nums` already includes history plus the current input; the generation resize counted that input again. Remove only this duplicate `+1`, retaining draft/extra reservations and the normal scheduler's generation growth. This lets CUDA-graph warmup use the capacity returned by the manager without skipping feasible batch shapes. `model_engine.py` is unchanged from main.

Original gRPC, Seed-OSS, Mistral, and multimodal-example fixtures explicitly select V2. A benchmark comment is corrected without changing its budget. No native allocator or public configuration changes.

## Test Coverage

The committed generic test changes retain the context constraint assertions and add one regression with draft lengths 0 and 4: query the available capacity, then allocate a generation dummy exactly at a page boundary. Both cases fail on the old dummy allocator and pass with the correction. The enclosing executor directory is already included in `l0_h100.yml`.

One CPU-only V4 configuration test covers the default ratio and an explicit pool ratio. It asserts the exact longest-decode-plus-minimal-decodes constraint (including draft/extra reservations), preserves the inherited context constraint, and checks the explicit-ratio opt-out. The existing `l0_cpu.yml` attention-directory entry collects its `cpu_only` marker. Diagnostic scripts and larger temporary matrices remain outside the PR.

Real B200 validation on September 22 PDT / September 23 UTC:

- V4 config regression: 2 passed with all GPUs hidden and CUDA uninitialized, loading the complete current V4 source and tracked test file against the compatible CI60862 runtime. A direct whole-branch run was blocked at import by the older native runtime lacking `StorageStatistics`.
- Native page-boundary regression: baseline 2 expected failures; fixed 2 passed.
- Qwen3-0.6B runtime trace: normal decode with history 31 grows capacity 31 -> 32. A dummy with the same history and one input allocated 33 before, 32 after; both send KV length 32 to attention. Capture/replay succeeds and greedy outputs are identical.
- Seed-OSS-36B: temporary and final caches each complete 34/34 graph warmups and captures, with no skipped shapes. Full 1,319-sample GSM8K passed at **92.077%**, threshold **87.597%**.
- Qwen3-8B + Qwen3-0.6B DraftTarget, explicit V2 target and separate draft managers, D=4, graphs enabled: passed exact greedy parity for both eight-token outputs. All 8 additional temporary native-budget/capture checks passed (9/9 total, zero skips).

The Seed pytest completed successfully and workers shut down cleanly; its outer temporary shell runner subsequently exited 2 because that script was edited while the long test ran. title: [https://nvbugs/6812588][fix] Stop unbindable IPv6 addresses from reaching disaggregated listeners
body:
## Description

Two independent places where an IPv6 address that cannot be bound reaches a `bind()` call in disaggregated serving. Same class of failure, different layers, so they are fixed together.

### 1. UCX gets a ULA from `getLocalIp` (C++)

`getLocalIpByNic` and `getLocalIpByHostname` (`cpp/tensorrt_llm/common/ipUtils.cpp`) returned the **first** address they came across, so which address family won was decided by `getifaddrs`' kernel ordering or by the resolver's RFC 6724 ordering rather than by anything this code chose. Neither function filters IPv6 unique-local addresses: they only reject `fe80::` and `::1`, and an address in `fc00::/7` is neither.

That address is what `NixlTransferAgent` advertises (`transferAgent.cpp`, `common::getLocalIp(common::getEnvNixlInterface(), mRank)`) and what ends up in a UCX TCP bind. When the winner is a ULA with no usable scope id:

```
bind(fd=127 addr=fdcd:8200:fd71:50ab:9d:62ff:feec:5416%0:0) failed: Cannot assign requested address
uct_iface_open(tcp/rdma_vf_rail0) failed: Input/output error
-> NIXL UCX backend creation failure
```

**Fix:** keep the IPv4 early return in both functions and remember the first usable IPv6 as a fallback, so IPv4 wins whenever the host has one. `getLocalIpByRemoteOrHostName` has always tried IPv4 before IPv6; this makes the other two agree with it. Each function keeps its existing filters (`0.0.0.0`, `127.0.0.1`, `fe80::`, `::1`) exactly as they were — only the family preference changes.

### 2. The coordinator listener lets uvicorn resolve the host (Python)

The coordinator was the only disaggregated listener that handed uvicorn a host string. The standalone server (`disaggregated()`) and the fleet workers (`_run_fleet_worker_impl`) both bind an `AF_INET` socket first and pass `sockets=[s]`; only `_serve_coordinator_and_fleet` let uvicorn call `loop.create_server()` on the name. A hostname whose AAAA record is link-local then resolves to `fe80::` with scope id 0, which the kernel always refuses:

```
OSError: [Errno 22] error while attempting to bind on address ('fe80::ac31:4bff:fee6:2d43', 8332, 0, 0): invalid argument
```

A link-local address is only bindable with a scope id, and a scope id can only be derived from an interface name — a resolved hostname cannot carry one, so this can never succeed. Verified locally:

```
iface=enp1s0f0np0 addr=fe80::1270:fdff:fef8:aab8 scope_id=2
  bind scope_id=0: OSError 22 Invalid argument
  bind scope_id=2: OK
```

**Fix:** bind the coordinator's socket the way the other two listeners bind theirs and hand it to uvicorn. The bind happens before the fleet is launched, so a port clash fails before there are child processes to clean up, and it reports the port holder with the same diagnostics as the other listeners.

No new configuration in either half. Operators who need to pin a specific NIC for NIXL already have `TRTLLM_NIXL_INTERFACE`.

## Scope

This removes two specific ways an unbindable address reaches a bind call. It does not address a cluster whose rail interfaces are genuinely misconfigured for the container — that remains a `UCX_NET_DEVICES` / `UCX_TLS` question, as the disaggregated-serving docs describe. The waivers associated with NVBug 6812588 are therefore **not** removed here; they should come off only once a run on the affected GB300 nodes is green.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/bindings/test_transfer_agent_bindings.py::TestNixlTransferAgent::test_listening_agent_advertises_ipv4` — a listening `NixlTransferAgent` advertises whatever `getLocalIp` picked, and `get_local_connection_info()` is already bound, so the test asserts the property the UCX bind depends on: on any host with a routable IPv4 address the advertised address is IPv4, not a bracketed IPv6 literal. Skips on an IPv6-only host, where the fallback is the correct answer rather than a regression.
- `tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_coordinator_worker.py::test_coordinator_tcp_listener_uses_the_prebound_socket` — the TCP listener must serve the caller's socket (and the UDS listener must not take one), with and without UDS enabled. The host passed in is the link-local literal from the traceback above.

I do not have a full build environment here, so neither new test has been run locally — CI is their first run. The changed C++ was syntax-checked (`g++ -fsyntax-only`) and the changed Python byte-compiles; `pre-commit` is clean on all five files.

- `tests/unittest/kv_cache_manager_v2_tests/test_streaming_kv_events.py`: Covers stored and removed events, multimodal payloads, backend validation, and parallelism constraints. This is a unit test; the parent test directory is listed in the CI test lists noted above.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

The Python KV cache manager backend is being removed, but the streaming KV-event publisher introduced by #17023 currently depends on Python-side KV manager events.

This change keeps streaming KV events available with the C++ KV cache manager V2 backend:

- Add a native `StreamingEventSink` that captures stored and removed block events as compact C++ DTOs.
- Expose batched DTO draining through nanobind.
- Translate the DTOs to Python `BlockStored` and `BlockRemoved` msgspec structures and reuse the existing serialization and publisher path.
- Select the native event lifecycle automatically when the C++ backend is active while preserving the Python backend behavior.
- Add unit coverage and update the KV-cache documentation.

The boundary intentionally remains semantic rather than serialized:

```text
C++ KV cache manager -> native event DTOs -> nanobind -> Python BlockStored/BlockRemoved -> existing publisher
```


## Multimodal wire compatibility

**Breaking change for V2 multimodal streaming consumers:** previously, streaming `token_ids` contained integers and digest-bearing blocks were suppressed. This PR can emit hexadecimal digest strings in `token_ids` and add `mm_keys` to `BlockStored`. Consumers that assume every token ID is an integer are incompatible. Text-only payloads are unchanged.

The final cross-project interface is still being finalized by [Dynamo #15095](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/15095) and [TensorRT-LLM #19529](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/19529). We will revisit multimodal streaming handling separately after both PRs merge, when the interface is finalized, rather than define that final contract in this DTO/backend PR.

title: [None][fix] Validate unused chat template controls and normalize router tool arguments
body:
## Description

A `chat_template_kwargs` key the active chat template never reads is a silent no-op: the request succeeds and the control is dropped on the floor. This PR adds a guard that statically analyzes the resolved Jinja template and rejects unused controls with a clear `ValueError` (mapped to a structured 400 on the server), with `TRTLLM_ALLOW_UNUSED_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS=1` as an escape hatch that downgrades the rejection to a once-per-(template, key) warning.

Details:
- New `tensorrt_llm/inputs/chat_template_guard.py`: conservative AST analysis (fails open on syntax errors, includes/imports, or anything it cannot fully analyze), understands transformers' `{% generation %}` tag, always allows standard renderer parameters and special-token overrides.
- Wired into both render entry points: `inputs/utils.apply_chat_template` (server path) and `serve/chat_tokenization.render_chat_request_for_tokenizer` (router/disaggregated tokenization path), so the router and the server agree on what a request means.
- The router path now applies the same assistant-message normalization as the server (tool-call `function.arguments` parsed from JSON strings), so both paths tokenize identical text for the same request.
- `resolve_hf_chat_template` resolves a named template selection against the tokenizer's template dict, so validation runs against the template that will actually render.

- Server-injected controls are exempt from the check. The Anthropic adapter and the Responses path add keys of their own (`clear_thinking`/`drop_thinking`, `reasoning_effort`/`thinking`) that the reasoning parsers consume regardless of the template. `validate_chat_template_kwargs` takes an `injected_keys` set, threaded through both render entry points; `ChatCompletionRequest.injected_chat_template_kwargs` carries it across the edge-to-worker relay so the router applies the same exemption. Caller-supplied keys stay strict. `enable_thinking` and `thinking` are always accepted because the reasoning parsers read them from `chat_template_kwargs` whether or not the template does.
- The guard raises `UnusedChatTemplateKwargsError` (a `ValueError`), and the disaggregated server maps it to HTTP 400 instead of falling into the generic 500 handler.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/llmapi/apps/test_chat_template_kwargs_guard.py` (cpu_only): guard semantics (referenced/unreferenced/self-defaulted variables, generation-tag templates, unparseable templates, escape hatch, cache isolation), wiring on both entry points, router/server tool-call tokenization parity, named-template selection.
- `tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_router.py`: router tokenization rejects kwargs the template never reads; existing forwarding test extended to a template that reads its kwargs.
