title: [#17714][feat] NcclEP: make algorithm/layout selectable so HIGH_THROUGHPUT+FLAT works on EFA
body:
## Description

Closes #17714.

The `NcclEP` MoE backend hardcodes `Algorithm.LOW_LATENCY` (`nccl_ep_utils.py`) and forces `Layout.RANK_MAJOR` at three layers (the `NcclEpContext` ctor default, `get_nccl_ep_context`, and `communication/nccl_ep.py::_get_context`). On AWS EFA the safe algorithm/layout tuple is fabric-dependent: the device-initiated `LOW_LATENCY` path takes a CUDA illegal memory access at first dispatch, while `HIGH_THROUGHPUT`+`FLAT` runs correctly (details and the both-ways substrate caveat in #17714).

This PR adds `TRTLLM_NCCL_EP_ALGO` (`LOW_LATENCY` | `HIGH_THROUGHPUT`, default `LOW_LATENCY` — behavior unchanged for existing users) and plumbs it through all three layout decision points; under HT the layout defaults to `FLAT` (the HT kernel asserts on `RANK_MAJOR`).

The HT/FLAT path also carries three buffer-contract differences the LL default never exercises, all gated on the same probe:

- 2D `[max_recv, hidden]` recv buffers (the HT kernel asserts `ndim==2`; LL keeps its 3D rank-major shape)
- int64 `recv_topk_idx` per the shipped v0.1 `nccl_ep.h` HT ABI, narrowed back to int32 at the dispatch return boundary because `torch.ops.trtllm.fused_moe` requires int32 routing ids (expert ids and the `-1` unrouted sentinel both fit; under LL the cast is a no-op)
- dispatch `layout_info=None` under HT (per `nccl_ep.h`: counters arrive via `ncclEpUpdateHandle`; `src_rank_counters` is an LL-rank-major-only field)

**Framing (honest):** this is an opt-in **correctness/enablement** change, not a performance win — at our measured shape native `nccl_ep` HT is ~3.7× slower than a CPU-proxy reference. The point is that users on fabrics where the hardcoded tuple faults currently have no way to select the tuple that works.

**Measured** on 2× p5en (16× H200) over AWS EFA, NCCL 2.30.4 + `nccl_ep` 0.1.0: 16/16 ranks × 3 rounds dispatch+combine correctness-checked PASS, plus a real `trtllm-serve` (Qwen3-30B-A3B, EP8) producing coherent, arithmetically-correct output. Default (`TRTLLM_NCCL_EP_ALGO` unset) leaves every code path byte-equivalent to today's behavior.

## Test Coverage

- Default-path inertness: with `TRTLLM_NCCL_EP_ALGO` unset, `NcclEpContext` resolves `LOW_LATENCY`+`RANK_MAJOR` exactly as before (existing NcclEP tests cover this path).
- HT/FLAT enablement was validated on live EFA hardware (16-rank correctness harness + real serve, above); the tuple is not exercisable in single-GPU CI. Happy to add a unit test asserting the env-gate → (algorithm, layout, buffer-shape, dtype) resolution logic without requiring multi-node fabric if reviewers want it.

## PR Checklist

- [x] PR description clearly explains what and why.
- [x] PR follows TRT-LLM coding guidelines to the best of my knowledge.
- [ ] ~~Test cases are provided for new code paths — resolved as deferred-on-request: default path covered by existing NcclEP tests, HT/FLAT tuple not exercisable in single-GPU CI; env-gate resolution unit test offered in Test Coverage, will add if reviewers want it.~~
- [x] No API change (env-var opt-in only; default behavior unchanged) — no `api-compatible`/`api-breaking` label needed.
- [x] No new dependencies.
- [x] No ownership/docs/architecture-diagram change.
- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

title: [None][feat] Add opt-in disaggregated transfer diagnostics
body:
## Why

Add opt-in, request-level evidence for admission/backpressure and KV-transfer ownership debugging following [#18150](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/18150). This PR observes existing behavior; it does not change admission, ownership, timeout policy, or transport messages.

## What changed

- Record admission/rollback, transfer-window decisions, KV pressure, readiness, queueing, submission/completion, settlement, timeout/cancellation, KV release, and decode readiness. Bypassed Gate 2 is observed only as a counterfactual.
- Consolidate request/rank metadata and timeout events in [shared helpers](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/d43a87d7078ee6ac93ff52e0734d5bcda0e0bf32/tensorrt_llm/_torch/disaggregation/diagnostics.py). Share one descriptor-local payload measurement with the existing [native performance logger](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/d43a87d7078ee6ac93ff52e0734d5bcda0e0bf32/tensorrt_llm/_torch/disaggregation/native/transfer.py); its enablement and timing semantics remain unchanged. RequestPerfMetrics continues owning aggregate request metrics.
- Use a bounded, asynchronous sink and an offline [analyzer](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/d43a87d7078ee6ac93ff52e0734d5bcda0e0bf32/scripts/disagg_transfer_diagnostics.py). Runtime/scheduler capabilities distinguish unsupported events from missing evidence; writer-cohort metadata handles attention-DP broadcasts.
- Correlate explicit disaggregated IDs across workers only within a shared run UUID. Fallback IDs remain process-local, and sessionless wire observations report unknown identity scope. Durations never cross process/clock domains.

## Usage and overhead

Diagnostics are **disabled by default**. Enable with `TRTLLM_DISAGG_TRANSFER_DIAGNOSTICS=1`. For cross-worker correlation, set `TRTLLM_DISAGG_TRANSFER_DIAGNOSTICS_RUN_ID` to the same fresh UUID on all CTX/GEN workers.

Disabled mode avoids diagnostic clock reads, request scans, UUID generation, serialization, queueing, and I/O; cheap flag checks and minimal bookkeeping remain. No measured zero-overhead claim is made. Enabled diagnostics are for targeted debugging, not authoritative throughput measurement, and do not enable the existing aggregate performance collectors.

The sink is bounded and best-effort. Queue/write losses are reported when possible; blocked/broken stdout or process exit can lose the final tail, and partial writes can produce malformed records. The analyzer reports incomplete/unknown evidence rather than inventing correlations.

## Validation

- Rebased onto main `1a36f4fed9`; current head: [`d43a87d707`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/commit/d43a87d7078ee6ac93ff52e0734d5bcda0e0bf32). Integration hooks/tests follow the current coordinator and native Chunk/CacheExtent/PeerFetch APIs.
- Added coordinator, lifecycle, payload-reuse, fallback-ID, and cleanup regression coverage, including disabled/enabled/failing diagnostics and independent performance-logger flags. A fresh end-to-end self-review found no remaining actionable issues.
- **106 analyzer tests passed.** **36 isolated sink/helper tests passed** using the actual diagnostic module without importing the unavailable application runtime; this is not a runtime-suite pass.
- Applicable pre-commit checks, Python compilation, test-list validation, pinned-memory policy, and whitespace checks passed. Runtime pytest collection is blocked locally by missing PyTorch; runtime/GPU integration and performance validation remain for CI.
- [Full CI requested](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/18913#issuecomment-5784837718) with `/bot run --disable-fail-fast`. [Jenkins launcher #75116](https://nv/trt-llm-cicd/job/helpers/job/PR_Github/75116/) has started for `d43a87d707`, with [full-CI pipeline #61869](https://nv/trt-llm-cicd/job/main/job/L0_MergeRequest_PR/61869/) dispatched; test results are pending. The PR currently lacks `ci: full pre-merge approved`, so gated multi-GPU coverage requires maintainer approval.

Earlier CI results validate older heads only.

title: [None][feat] Add opt-in per-request cached KV token logging
body:
## Description

Iteration logs expose only the sum of cached KV tokens, making it difficult to inspect individual cached-prefix lengths in a disaggregated GEN batch. Set `TLLM_LOG_CACHED_KV_TOKENS_PER_REQ=1` before starting workers to add `cached_kv_tokens_per_req` to the existing `states` log. The flag is read once during model-engine initialization and defaults to off.

The list follows model-input sequence order and excludes CUDA graph padding requests. Filtering follows the context, extend, first-draft, and generation groups used by input preparation, including beam expansion. This handles padding inside the packed MTP batch and preserves all real beam entries. The normal input, steady-generation, and encoder-decoder fast paths all update the diagnostic. Attention-DP dummy rows remain part of the scheduled-input accounting.

The existing `cached_kv_tokens` total retains its original semantics. The companion `cached_kv_tokens_cuda_graph_padding` field reports the excluded contribution, so:

```text
cached_kv_tokens = sum(cached_kv_tokens_per_req) + cached_kv_tokens_cuda_graph_padding
```

For example, `[100, 200]` with a padding contribution of `7` corresponds to a total of `307`. With beam width 1, each retained entry corresponds to one scheduled request; multiple beams produce per-sequence entries. These are cached-prefix token counts, not physical KV-cache occupancy.

Disabled mode does not traverse requests, copy counts, or format the extra fields. Enabled mode adds CPU filtering and logging without new CUDA synchronization.

## Test Coverage

- Added 8 regression tests in `TestCachedKvTokenLogging`: encoder-decoder padding, MTP padding before real rows, multiple beams, promoted context order, attention-DP dummy preservation, padding-only batches, and stale-value cleanup on steady/empty batches. The tests also check snapshot independence and total reconciliation.
- Locally executed those 8 tests against the actual helper in an isolated CPU source harness, plus 18 cases exercising the actual flag initialization and all three logging call sites with the environment unset/0/1. Full TensorRT-LLM test-module imports and GPU inference were not run locally.
- Python syntax compilation, `git diff --check`, repository pre-commit checks, and DCO validation.

title: [None][fix] Bound DSpark scratch positions across graph replays
body:
## Description

The embedded DSpark worker shares a reserved slot among CUDA graph padding and attention-DP idle requests. Its decode position currently accumulates across generation steps for the lifetime of the worker. Eventually, RoPE gathers can index past their fixed table even though the dummy rows are subsequently masked.

Reset the scratch slot's previous position to zero inside `_advance_generation_state()` using tensor operations, so the reset executes on every CUDA graph replay without host synchronization. Real-request position bootstrap and advancement retain their existing behavior. This adds one tensor comparison/selection to the generation path; full-serving performance has not been measured for this upstream adaptation.

## Test Coverage

Added `test_dspark_generation_state.py` under the existing `hw_agnostic` directory, already included by the CPU and H100 CI lists:

- CPU: initialized and uninitialized scratch positions at/beyond the RoPE boundary, duplicate scratch rows with different accepted-token counts, repeated advancement, real-request bootstrap, and recycled real-slot state.
- CUDA: capture/replay with changing real/scratch mappings and accepted-token counts for batches 16, 32, 48, 64, 96, and 128, followed by 1,000 all-padding replays.

Validation performed locally on macOS with PyTorch 2.8.0:
- Invoked the two CPU regression cases using the actual `_advance_generation_state` method extracted from upstream source via AST, isolating it from unavailable TensorRT-LLM runtime dependencies. Both fail with out-of-bounds indexing on unpatched main and pass with the fix.
- Ruff 0.9.4 lint and formatting checks pass for both changed files.
- `git diff --check` passes.

The full upstream pytest suite, pre-commit suite, and CUDA replay tests have not been run in this environment. GPU CI validation is pending.

## Summary

The `OpenAIDisaggServer` (disaggregated proxy) does not implement the `/v1/models` endpoint, causing incompatibility with standard OpenAI API clients such as the OpenAI Python SDK, LangChain, and other tools that rely on this endpoint for model discovery.

**Current behavior:**
```
curl http://localhost:8100/v1/models
# Returns: {"detail":"Not Found"}
```

**After this change:**
```
curl http://localhost:8100/v1/models
# Returns: {"object":"list","data":[{"id":"model-name","object":"model","created":...,"owned_by":"tensorrt_llm"}]}
```

- Import `ModelCard` and `ModelList` from `openai_protocol`

- Add `get_models()` handler that extracts the model name from the server configuration and returns an OpenAI API-compatible `ModelList` response

This mirrors the existing `/v1/models` implementation in `OpenAIServer`, adapted for the disaggregated proxy which reads the model path from `DisaggServerConfig.server_configs`.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

DFlash's pooled-context K/V buffers are allocated lazily during warmup, after the KV-cache pool has committed, so sizing mistakes fail late and opaquely: an oversized `max_batch_size` dies as a bare CUDA OOM, and a violated token budget (`max_batch_size * (1 + max_draft_len) > max_num_tokens`) corrupts memory at engine init. This PR has two commits:

**Commit 1 — config-time budget validation and sizing/position fixes:**
- `validate_dflash_ctx_buffer_budget` (called from `TorchLlmArgs.validate_speculative_config` for DFlash) turns both failure modes into config-time errors: it enforces the token-budget rule and estimates the pooled-context buffer footprint against the memory left after the KV pool commits. The budget subtracts an estimate of the per-rank weight footprint (checkpoint shard bytes across TP x PP ranks) before applying `(1 - free_gpu_memory_fraction)`; budgeting against the device total blesses batch sizes that then OOM in warmup. Refusals name the largest fitting `max_batch_size`.
- Buffer capacity is `min(max_seq_len, max_position_embeddings)` — the same clamp the lazy allocation applies. Sizing off `max_position_embeddings` alone made 1M-position drafters refuse batch sizes their serve shape fits with room to spare (~21x over-budget at a 49152 serve length).
- The context arena reads the served length from `attn_metadata.kv_cache_manager.max_seq_len`, which every backend carries, instead of a `max_seq_len` attribute only some metadata classes declare. On FlashInfer the attribute read came back empty and the arena was sized for the drafter's advertised 1048576 positions (a 165 GiB allocation, OOM in the first warmup forward) instead of the served 49152.
- RoPE drafter prefill context is written at slot-local positions: on a prefix-cache hit the target-forward positions start at the reused-token count, which would offset every stored key from the numbering the draft queries use.

**Commit 2 — FlashInfer one-engine speculation gate as a qualification boundary:**
The FLASHINFER one-engine speculation check refused every one-engine mode that does not share the target KV cache, with a message claiming a capability gap. That predicate is too broad (it refuses modes that need no separate draft KV cache manager at all — the suffix automaton, and DFlash's VANILLA/FA4 draft backends with worker-owned private buffers) and inaccurately stated for DFlash, where the refusal is a qualification decision: the combination boots and generates at a small batch size but has not been qualified at serving scale. `_flashinfer_one_engine_spec_supported` refuses DFlash regardless of draft backend or cache ownership, admits one-engine modes that need no separate draft manager, and states the qualification grounds plus the remedy (TRTLLM target attention).

## Test Coverage

All CPU-only:
- `tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/hw_agnostic/test_dflash_config_budget.py` (new): the buffer-bytes formula (VANILLA and TRTLLM paged layouts), budget derivation and weight-shard estimate, the config-time refusals with fitting-value messaging, the trained-width warning, and the `TorchLlmArgs` wiring including the weight-subtraction path.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/hw_agnostic/test_dflash_ctx_arena_sizing.py` (new): the arena sizing decision on metadata with and without the `max_seq_len` attribute, agreement between backends, and the position table remaining a ceiling.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_py_executor_creator_flashinfer_spec_gate.py` (new): DFlash pinned as refused on FLASHINFER for every draft backend and cache-ownership setting; admission of no-speculation, shared-cache, external-drafter, and suffix-automaton configurations; other backends ungated.

title: [None][fix] Gate disaggregated KV block reuse admission on verified write coverage
body:
## Description

In disaggregated serving, the generation worker admits the KV block range it
received from the context worker into the block-reuse (radix) tree once the
transfer reports SUCCESS. A SUCCESS result alone is not proof that the
destination pages were actually written: a write that is skipped, partial, or
misrouted while a SUCCESS result frame is still delivered would put
never-written pages into the reuse tree under the prompt's token hashes, and
any later request sharing that prefix would silently reuse the poisoned
blocks (cross-request contamination). The failure is silent because the
original request itself is unaffected — only future reuse hits are wrong.

This change makes reuse admission fail-closed on verified write coverage:

- **Sender attestation** (`native/transfer.py`, `Sender._deliver_kv_to_agent`):
  the `transfer_size` carried in each KV result frame now attests only bytes
  from a submission that actually completed (`write_meta.sizes.sum()`), and is
  0 otherwise — never intent. Previously it was populated only when perf
  logging was on.
- **Receiver accounting** (`native/transfer.py`, `KVRecvTask` / `RxSession`):
  each receive task records the expected byte total of its published
  destinations (`expected_write_bytes`) and accumulates the writers' attested
  bytes; `write_verified` requires strict equality (over-coverage means
  duplicated/misrouted writes and is as disqualifying as missing coverage).
  `RxSession.kv_write_verified()` is the per-rank admission predicate.
- **Plumbing** (`base/transfer.py`, `native/fetch.py`, `transceiver.py`): the
  transceiver computes the local destination byte total
  (`_chunk_num_bytes(extent.local)`) and passes it through
  `PeerFetch.fetch(..., expected_write_bytes=...)` into `RxSession.receive`.
- **Cross-rank consensus** (`transceiver.py`): per-rank reuse trees stay
  consistent only if every rank admits the same tokens, so the verified
  verdict is intersected across ranks in the existing batched outcome
  allgather (one extra id list, no extra collective).
- **Fail-closed commit gate** (`transceiver.py`,
  `commit_blocks_for_reuse`): the received range is committed to the reuse
  tree only when the request carries a positive verified verdict
  (`py_kv_transfer_verified`); a missing verdict is treated as unverified.
  Skipping the commit never affects the request itself — generation proceeds
  normally, the blocks just stay out of the reuse tree — so the gate can only
  trade a reuse hit for correctness.

## Test Coverage

New: `tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_verified_reuse_admission.py`
(cpu-only, mock-based):

- `KVRecvTask.write_verified`: exact coverage verifies; short, over, and
  unknown-expected coverage do not; empty transfer (fully cached prefix)
  verifies trivially; untransferred task never verifies.
- `RxSession` accounting: expected bytes plumb into the task; multi-writer
  SUCCESS results accumulate attested bytes; a SUCCESS result with zero
  attested bytes (the false-success case) leaves the session unverified even
  though the transfer looks complete; partial coverage and FAILED-result
  bytes do not verify; an empty session is never verified.
- Commit gate: verified request commits to the reuse adapter; unverified or
  missing verdict does not.
- Cross-rank consensus: a request is verified only when every rank verified
  its shard; the no-sync path uses the local verdict; the quiesced-only call
  shape used by the context path is unchanged.
- Sender attestation: a completed submission attests the actual byte total in
  the result frame; a failed submission attests zero.

Updated: `tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_transfer_ownership_regressions.py`
for the widened consensus outcome list and the new `receive` parameter.

title: [nvbugs/6758245] Avoid metrics queue polling when iteration stats are disabled
body:
## Rubin issue
NVBug 6758245 reports that Kimi K3 NVFP4 serving on Rubin regresses when `enable_iter_perf_stats=false`: output performance and interactivity degrade versus the enabled configuration. The failure is in the disabled `/metrics` path, not in metric computation.

## Root cause / invariant
With iteration stats disabled, no background stats buffer is created. The `/metrics` handler nevertheless fell through to the legacy `get_stats_async(2)` queue poll, causing a timeout/poll on every request. With stats enabled, the collector-owned buffer path was used. The invariant is that disabled stats must return an empty metrics payload without touching the stats queue, while VisualGen, enabled buffered metrics, and legacy missing-flag behavior remain unchanged.

## Change
- Short-circuit disabled iteration stats in `OpenAIServer.get_iteration_stats`.
- Add repeated direct-call and registered FastAPI `/metrics` regression coverage.

## Evidence
The Rubin reproduction recorded the false arm entering `legacy_queue_poll` with `get_stats_async(2)` and the true arm using `buffer_return`; after the guard, the false arm is `disabled_short_circuit`.

## Validation
- Commit `4ccb3fdf8c5facc9dbf4a77e40cde19d71dc4141` reviewed and transplanted as `c5854eab343ba78a70ab81c01e1ae13866d85b4a`.
- Compile, Ruff formatting/checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Codex adversarial review found no actionable correctness issues.

## Description

LLM.encode() accepts model-specific tensors via `**model_kwargs`, but the encoder runner rejected them whenever encoder CUDA graphs were enabled, so models needing an extra input had to give up graph capture.

This PR replaces that rejection with a declaration. Each tensor `kwarg` is declared in `EncodeCudaGraphConfig.extra_model_inputs`; the runner gives it a static buffer, captures every bucket with a zero-filled stand-in so the graph sees the full `forward()` signature, and copies the caller's tensor into the buffer on each replay (zero-filling the padding tail).

A spec has exactly one symbolic dimension, which is what lets it cover every bucket:

- "`num_tokens`" — scales with the packed token count (e.g. `token_type_ids`)
- "`batch_size`" — one row per request (e.g. per-request features)

Other dimensions are fixed integers. Before `forward()`, a declared `kwarg` must be a tensor matching its spec; an undeclared tensor raises (almost always a forgotten spec, and falling back silently would hide the lost speedup), while an undeclared non-tensor runs that call eagerly instead of being frozen into the graph at its capture-time value. Tensors may be on host or device.

## Example

```python
from tensorrt_llm import LLM
from tensorrt_llm.llmapi import EncodeCudaGraphConfig, EncodeExtraInputSpec

cuda_graph_config = EncodeCudaGraphConfig(
    batch_sizes=[1, 2, 4],
    num_tokens=[64, 128],
    seq_lens=[32, 64],
    enable_padding=True,
    extra_model_inputs=[
        EncodeExtraInputSpec(name="token_type_ids", shape=("num_tokens",), dtype="int32"),
        EncodeExtraInputSpec(name="per_request_feature", shape=("batch_size", 20), dtype="float32"),
    ],
)

llm = LLM(model=MODEL, encode_only=True, cuda_graph_config=cuda_graph_config)

outputs = llm.encode(
    prompts,
    token_type_ids=token_type_ids,     # (total_tokens,) int32
    per_request_feature=per_request_feats,  # (len(prompts), 20) float32
)
```

### Not supported

`extra_model_inputs` is rejected for feature-mode and encoder-decoder encoder graphs.

title: [https://nvbugs/6665906][fix] Restore Mistral Large 3 multimodal inference
body:
## Description

The verified NVBug 6665906 startup failure is caused by `checkpoint_format="mistral_large_3"` selecting `MistralNativeInputProcessor` while `Mistral3VLM` advertises multimodal encoder item scheduling. The native processor did not implement the required scheduling hooks, so engine construction failed before inference.

Static analysis also identifies a follow-on required by this model geometry: Mistral-Large-3 uses a 1664 / 16 = 104 Pixtral attention head. TRTLLM-GEN does not support head size 104, so SM100 must route that exact shape to FMHA v2. FMHA v2 must generate both the head-dimension-104 kernel and its packed-QKV padding-mask variant. This follow-on has not yet been observed in a GB200 run because the verified startup failure occurs first.

This change:

- shares the Pixtral encoder item-scheduling contract between the Hugging Face and mistral-native input processors
- adds head size 104 beside the existing head size 72 SM100 fallback to FMHA v2
- generates the SM100 head-dimension-104 kernel and keeps the packed-QKV padding-mask allowlist synchronized
- adds CPU generator and processor-contract coverage and removes the NVBug waiver

Adding 104 to the padding-mask allowlist also enables the same Pixtral-Large fused shape on the existing SM80/86/89/90/120 FMHA v2 families. This is intentional coverage of the same model geometry, not a separate behavior change.

The NVBug 6572838 change is not sufficient here because it disables the multimodal encoder for text-only tests; this MMMU case requires the vision encoder.

title: [TRTLLMINF-336][infra] Publish the BOLTed build under a distinct name
body:
## Description

The canonical-overwrite scheme cannot be made race-free. The canonical SBSA tarball is
downloadable the moment `Build-SBSA` finishes, and `Build-Docker-Images` runs in parallel
with the SBSA branch, so `get_wheel_from_package.py` fetches it hours before `BoltProfileGen`
could replace it. The image then contains the unoptimized wheel permanently, even when BOLT
later succeeds, and nothing about the run says so. `Dockerfile.bolt` does not close that gap
either -- it copies profiles into the image, it does not optimize the installed binaries.

This publishes the optimized build as `bolted-<tarball>` instead, a second object next to an
untouched canonical one. The artifact is its own publication signal: it appears atomically
and only on success, so a consumer that names it either gets optimized bytes or gets nothing
to fetch. Consumers that require optimization name it explicitly and fail when it is absent
(wired up separately); consumers that do not care keep reading the canonical object, which
now never changes under them.

Two things fall out:

- The input is unambiguous. Canonical is the un-BOLTed build by construction, on a fresh
  `artifactPath` and on a re-run alike, so the `unbolted-<tarball>` snapshot and the probe
  that preferred it exist only to prevent a double-BOLT that can no longer happen. Both go away.
- The SBSA test stages, which are sequenced after `BOLT-Profile-Gen`, now prefer
  `bolted-<tarball>` when it is there, so post-merge still exercises the very build the run
  promotes. They fall back to canonical loudly -- that is all that exists on x86, on pre-merge,
  and when the producer did not publish.

`Build.groovy`'s pre-merge path keeps naming its BOLTed tarball canonical: it runs before the
upload, so that object is written once, already optimized, and no consumer can have fetched
an earlier version of it.

**Renames the job parameter** `boltPublishCanonical` -> `boltPublishBolted`. Because the
`parameters{}` block replaces the job's parameter list on every run, an undeclared parameter
is dropped even when the parent sends it -- so the first post-merge run after this lands
publishes nothing. Harmless (publication is still off), but worth knowing.

Still default OFF; the rollout is flipped on in #19209.

## Test Coverage

No automated tests -- this is CI infrastructure, and the publish path is dead code until the
toggle in #19209 lands, so this PR is a no-op on `main`.

What to look for on a `/bot run`: the SBSA test stages log
`[BOLT] no bolted-<tarball> ... (HTTP 404); testing the canonical un-BOLTed build`
and download exactly as before. The `BoltProfileGen` stage logs
`PUBLISH_BOLTED_TARBALL=false: not publishing a BOLTed tarball.`

The publish path itself is first exercised by #19209.

Renames the job parameter boltPublishCanonical -> boltPublishBolted. Still default OFF; the rollout is flipped on in a follow-up change.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Publishes optimized artifacts as `bolted-<tarball>` without overwriting the canonical artifact after merge.
- Publishes only when `boltPublishBolted`, profile application, and promotion are enabled.
- SBSA stages prefer the bolted artifact and fall back to the canonical artifact.
- `jenkins/Build.groovy` still creates and uploads `unbolted-<tarball>` during pre-merge consumption. This conflicts with the stated removal of the unbolted snapshot and requires confirmation.
- Review findings and test results were not supplied.

## QA Engineer Review

No test changes.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- **`jenkins/BoltProfileGen.groovy`**: Verify separate bolted publication, canonical artifact preservation, missing-output handling, publication conditions, and the renamed parameter default.
- **`jenkins/Build.groovy`**: Verify the pre-merge path and confirm whether `unbolted-<tarball>` must remain. Current logic preserves and uploads this artifact.
- **`jenkins/L0_Test.groovy`**: Verify bolted-artifact probing, retries, HTTP-status handling, fallback behavior, and artifact selection in both test paths.

title: [TRTLLMINF-336][infra] Apply BOLT to the released SBSA wheel
body:
## Description

The released SBSA manylinux wheel is not optimized today. `L0_Test.groovy::runLLMBuild()`
compiles it separately from the packed tarball and uploads it straight to `<arch>/`, and
`ENABLE_BOLT_COMPATIBLE=ON` only makes those binaries BOLT-able -- it does not apply the
optimization. The tarball gets BOLTed elsewhere (`Build.groovy` pre-merge, `BoltProfileGen`
post-merge), so the wheel was the one release artifact with no path to it at all.

`apply_bolt.py` already knew how to BOLT a wheel and regenerate its `RECORD`; that code was
only reachable for wheels packed inside a release tarball. This adds a `--wheel` mode that
reuses `process_wheel()` on a standalone `.whl`, and teaches `apply_latest.sh` to pick
tarball-vs-wheel mode from the input extension. `--manifest` stays tarball-only: it verifies
ELF hashes against the release layout, which a bare wheel has no tree for.

`runLLMBuild()` then applies the branch's latest promoted bundle in place, before the upload
and before the local pip install and the DLFW repack, so every consumer sees the same bytes.

**Scope.** aarch64 with an empty `wheel_path`, i.e. the wheel published at the root of
`<arch>/` that the release job picks up. An `imageTest/` build is a throwaway wheel compiled
inside an already-released image to prove that image can still build from source, so
optimizing it would prove nothing and only add a failure mode.

**Failure handling** mirrors `Build.groovy::applyLatestBolt`. A real apply error is always
fatal -- never upload a half-BOLTed wheel. A *missing* bundle is the cold-start case and is
fatal only for a `nightly_release` run, whose wheels the release job actually publishes;
otherwise it is a loud skip, so cutting a new branch does not start failing every
sanity-check build.

## Test Coverage

No automated tests -- this is CI infrastructure. Verified locally against a synthetic wheel
with a stubbed `llvm-bolt`:

- the profiled lib changes, the unprofiled one does not
- every `RECORD` row's hash and size still match the archive contents after repack
- the input wheel is left untouched (a failed apply leaves it uploadable)
- `apply_latest.sh` returns 0 / 3 / 2 on apply, missing bundle, and apply error respectively,
  and tarball inputs still take the `--tarball --manifest` path

In CI this is exercised by the SBSA `PackageSanityCheck` stages, which build and upload the
wheel this change now BOLTs.

- Centralizes `LLVM_BOLT_VERSION` resolution and preserves environment overrides.

title: [TRTLLMINF-336][infra] Allow the SBSA release image to require the BOLTed wheel
body:
## Description

`boltOverlayEnabled` and `boltProfilesRequired` only govern the profile *bundle* baked in as
a thin `Dockerfile.bolt` layer, which documents how to reproduce a BOLTed build but leaves
the binaries the image actually installs unoptimized. Nothing governs the installed wheel,
and the tarball it comes from is whichever one exists first -- the canonical, unoptimized
one, since `Build-Docker-Images` runs in parallel with the SBSA branch.

This adds `boltRequireBoltedWheel`. When set, the SBSA release image is built from
`bolted-<tarball>` (`get_wheel_from_package.py --bolted`) rather than the canonical tarball,
waiting for it to be published and failing if it never is. Kept independent of the overlay
flags so it can be rolled back on its own, and scoped to `sbsa` because x86_64 has no
promoted bundle to wait for.

Two supporting changes:

- The wait gets its own, much longer clock. The canonical tarball lands when the build stage
  finishes; the BOLTed one only after `BoltProfileGen`'s SLURM fan-out, whose own stage
  timeout is 8h -- so 60 minutes is the wrong budget for it.
- The retry that rebuilds the wheel from source when a build fails with the download args is
  disabled for this path. It is a fine recovery for an ordinary build, but here it would
  silently produce an unoptimized release image that looks identical to an optimized one.

Also pins `wget`'s output name in the download loop. Without `-O` it falls back to `<name>.1`
when a previous attempt left a partial file behind, and the extract would then read stale
bytes -- a latent bug that gets much more reachable now that the loop can run for hours.

Default false, so this is inert until the toggle PR turns it on.

## Test Coverage

No automated tests -- this is CI infrastructure, and with `boltRequireBoltedWheel` defaulting
to false this PR is a no-op on `main`: `prepareWheelFromBuildStage` returns exactly the same
`BUILD_WHEEL_ARGS` as today, and the from-source retry behaves exactly as today.

`get_wheel_from_package.py --bolted` is a one-line name change (`bolted-` prefix) on top of
the existing, already-exercised download-and-extract path.

The enabled path is first exercised by the toggle PR.

title: [#19172][fix] Fix prompt embedding table H2D source lifetime
body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved reliability of asynchronous prompt-tuning data transfers by retaining source buffers until GPU copies complete.
  * Added safer handling for pending transfers during cleanup and shutdown.
  * Added CUDA event completion tracking for synchronization.

* **Tests**
  * Added coverage verifying prompt-embedding data remains available until asynchronous transfers finish.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

[#19172][fix] Fix prompt embedding table H2D source lifetime
Co-authored-by: OpenAI Codex <codex@openai.com>

## Description

Fixes #19172

## Problem

`BufferManager::copyFrom` performs host-to-device copies asynchronously.
After moving a request's prompt embedding table to the GPU, `LlmRequest`
immediately dropped its reference to the pooled-pinned host tensor.

If the request was cancelled, destroyed, or otherwise released before the
H2D completed, the pinned pool could reuse and overwrite the source while
CUDA was still consuming it.

## Impact

Under high GPU concurrency, especially with a competing GPU sidecar,
scheduling delays enlarged this race window. The copied prompt embeddings
could become corrupted, producing nondeterministic output and random early
EOS even in greedy decoding.

The issue affects the non-offloaded prompt embedding table path when the
source is held in the reusable pinned-memory pool.

## Root cause

Three individually reasonable lifetime assumptions interacted incorrectly:

- `BufferManager` queues the copy asynchronously and requires the caller to
  keep the source alive.
- The pinned pool permits a released allocation to be reused immediately.
- `LlmRequest` replaced and released its host tensor without tracking H2D
  completion.

## Fix

- Retain the host tensor in `PromptTuningBuffers` before queueing the H2D.
- Record a CUDA event immediately after the copy.
- Poll events nonblockingly during subsequent buffer preparation.
- Release each source only after its event reports completion.
- During destruction, wait only on the exact copy events rather than the
  entire runtime stream.
- Quarantine the source on exceptional paths where completion cannot be
  proven.

Request cancellation and destruction remain nonblocking.

## Testing

Added a deterministic regression test that gates the CUDA stream and
verifies:

1. The request can release its prompt embedding table without releasing the
   H2D source.
2. An incomplete-event cleanup poll retains the source.
3. The source is released after the copy event completes.

Local CUDA tests were not run because this checkout has no configured C++
CUDA test build.

title: [None][perf] DSv4 FP4 scorer + GVR V2 top-k: block-max skip, scorer pipeline, shape-gated PDL
body:
## Summary

When the skip is armed, the FP4 paged-MQA scorer emits one maximum per 32 compressed positions; the GVR V2 top-k derives an exact first-attempt line from them and scans only the surviving blocks. The scorer gets a 5-stage KV pipeline, a shorter prologue and a deferred logits store; both kernels take PDL where the shape pays.

Production-form scorer -> top-k chain vs origin/main on real DSv4 rows (geomean main / PR): pro 1.07–1.10 and flash 1.07–1.09 where the skip is armed (512k B >= 256, 1000k B >= 128), 1.02–1.12 over all 28 cells, exact throughout. DSv4 FP4 decode only.

## What changes

- **Block skip in the GVR V2 top-k** (single-CTA streaming main, 2-CTA cluster family): the first-attempt line is one histogram bin below the K-th largest block max, so `count(x >= line) >= K` holds by construction; surviving blocks are compacted into a per-CTA list and scanned as dense tiles. The verify-and-retry ladder is unchanged, so exactness never depends on the line; if no line can be formed the kernel uses the sampled line, and launches the gate does not arm run the existing dense path.
- **`block_max` emission in the FP4 scorer**, only when armed: one fp32 record per 32 positions (`[rows, nb_pad*4]`, `-FLT_MAX` padding), reduced and stored in the next tile's TMEM-load shadow; the plain build is unchanged.
- **Scorer pipeline and prologue**: 5 KV TMA stages, single-thread schedule-row load with shared-memory broadcast, first page indices fetched before the Q TMA, a second TMEM accumulator stage for `next_n == 1`, ReLU as `(x + |x|) * (w / 2)` with the 0.5 folded exactly into the weights, deferred logits store. Logits and `block_max` stay bit-identical to origin/main.
- **SPLIT line-miss robustness**: stratified jitter on the one-shot line sample, 32768 slab entries per row, a miss costs one whole-row float4 re-stage instead of whole-row radix narrowing; the miss floor is read only where it is published.
- **Shape-gated PDL** for the scorer -> top-k pair: the scorer waits at entry and triggers at the tile-loop exit; the varlen main / SPLIT top-k engines wait after their row prologue, the cluster and register engines before their first global read; armed only at rows <= 16 or npad <= 16384, otherwise codegen is identical to the PDL-off build.
- **Opt-in, default off**: a tail-only work-stealing scorer schedule (`TRTLLM_DSL_FP4_DYN_SCHED`, static cubin byte-identical) and a trimmed eager-mode host path (the static launch passes 10 positional arguments instead of 22; behaviour unchanged).

## Enablement and dispatch

| path | condition | default | knob | fallback |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Block skip (`block_max` emitted, top-k skips) | varlen decode on the single-CTA streaming main with `120 * K <= n <= 262144` and `rows * n * 4 B >= 96 MB`; the 2-CTA cluster family at `n = 262144` under the same footprint gate | on where the gate holds | `TRTLLM_GVR_BLOCK_SKIP_MIN_N_PER_K` = 120, `TRTLLM_GVR_BLOCK_SKIP_MIN_MB` = 96 | dense V2 scan, no `block_max` |
| Block-max line / compacted survivor scan | skip armed | on | `TRTLLM_GVR_BM_LINE` = 1, `TRTLLM_GVR_SKIP_COMPACT` = 1 | sampled line / byte-gated dense tiles |
| PDL on the scorer -> top-k pair | `TRTLLM_ENABLE_PDL` = 1 and (rows <= 16 or npad <= 16384) | on for small batch or short rows | `TRTLLM_GVR_PDL_MAX_B` = 16, `TRTLLM_GVR_PDL_MAX_NPAD` = 16384 | non-programmatic launch, same codegen |
| Scorer KV pipeline depth | always | 5 stages | `TRTLLM_DSL_FP4_KV_STAGES` | n/a |
| Scorer tail-only work stealing | `TRTLLM_DSL_FP4_DYN_SCHED` = 1 | off (`auto` resolves to off) | `TRTLLM_DSL_FP4_DYN_SCHED`, `_NMIN` = 384, `_HOST_NMIN` = 640, `_TAIL` = 2, `_CHUNK` = 16 | static schedule |

## Validation

At a glance: main / PR chain 1.07–1.10 (pro) and 1.07–1.09 (flash) in the skip-armed cells, 1.02–1.12 over all 28 cells; scorer alone 1.03–1.13 everywhere, top-k alone 1.35–3.09 (pro) / 2.04–3.56 (flash) where armed.
Exact: 1,663,305 / 1,663,305 campaign checks; 196,608 / 196,608 rows per model and arm in the head-to-head; scorer bit-exact vs origin/main 18 / 18; 207 + 1068 + 24 unit tests green as an overlay and as the installed wheel.

**Head-to-head vs origin/main 3b3cbc436f** (B200, both arms of a model on one GPU; main arm = origin/main scorer + V2 top-k, PR arm = a1d9a73be9, both as Python overlays on the `tensorrt_llm-1.3.0rc28` wheel whose C++ is identical to main; production form on rank-0-gated `campaign_g0` captures: scorer on each row's real `q.fp8` / `q.scale` / `weights` / `kfull` pages, top-k on the scorer's own logits, no copy kernel; 2048 distinct rows per ISL, fresh B distinct rows per replay; CUDA graph with a 192 MB L2 flush before every replay; replays 1024 / 256 / 48 at B 1 / 8 / >= 64; PDL off; nsys node-trace kernel durations; geomean of per-replay ratios). Bold = skip armed.

| N \ B | 1 | 8 | 64 | 128 | 256 | 512 | 1024 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pro 512k | 1.04 | 1.07 | 1.04 | 1.04 | **1.07** | **1.07** | **1.07** |
| pro 1000k | 1.07 | 1.12 | 1.04 | **1.07** | **1.10** | **1.10** | **1.10** |
| flash 512k | 1.07 | 1.07 | 1.04 | 1.02 | **1.08** | **1.09** | **1.09** |
| flash 1000k | 1.04 | 1.06 | 1.03 | **1.07** | **1.08** | **1.09** | **1.09** |

title: [TRTLLMINF-336][infra] Enable the BOLTed wheel for the SBSA release image
body:
## Description

Passes `boltRequireBoltedWheel=true` from both `BuildDockerImages` launches, so the SBSA
release image is built from `bolted-<tarball>` instead of racing the canonical tarball and
permanently baking in the unoptimized wheel. Both launches are set together because they push
the same tags: the scanned and registered artifact has to be the same image the post-merge
path publishes.

The scaffolding landed inert in the previous PR, so this only changes the answer to "should
this pipeline require the optimized build".

### Rollback

Drop `boltRequireBoltedWheel` from both launches, or set the job parameter to false. Nothing
else has to change: the canonical tarball is untouched by BOLT, so the image falls straight
back to it.

## Test Coverage

No automated tests -- this is CI infrastructure.

On a post-merge run, the `make ngc-release_push (sbsa)` stage should log
`Release image for sbsa requires the BOLT-optimized build; waiting up to 480 minutes for it`
and then `Tarfile is available at .../bolted-TensorRT-LLM-GH200.tar.gz`. x86_64 is unaffected
and still takes the canonical tarball.

The failure mode to watch on the first run is the wait itself: if `BoltProfileGen` fails, the
image build waits out its timeout and then fails rather than silently shipping an unoptimized
image. That is the intended behavior, and it is the reason for the operational note above.

title: [https://nvbugs/6732110][fix] Cache the split communicator in a new `MNNVLAllReduce.allreduce_mnnvl_pending_c…
body:
## Summary
- **Root cause**: The MNNVL workspace is published only after fabric allocation succeeds, so a failed `McastGPUBuffer` construction leaves the cache empty and every later `AllReduce` module issues another world-wide `mpi_comm().Split()`, leaking one communicator per layer until MPI communicator resources are exhausted and ranks die asymmetrically.
- **Fix**: Cache the split communicator in a new `MNNVLAllReduce.allreduce_mnnvl_pending_comms` ClassVar, reuse it on retry, and hand ownership to the workspace at publish time so the checkpoint hooks stay byte-identical to upstream; construction retries are preserved (9→9).
- **Original test**: `python .repair-bot/repro.py`
- Automated fix generated by repair-bot

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/attention/backends/sparse/qsa/cache_manager.py`: Verify that QSA index-key and position buffers remain consistent when draft reuse backoff is disabled.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/_util.py`: Verify pairing gates and draft-aware cache sizing, layer masks, and target-only state handling.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/kv_cache/kv_cache_manager_v2.py`: Verify role-specific backoff, draft publication gating, advisory lookahead handling, and draft capacity reserves.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/kv_cache/mamba_cache_manager.py`: Verify that draft pools use base commit and context-resource paths, while target pools preserve snapshot-boundary commits and recurrent-state updates.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_joint_reuse_pairing.py`: Verify the four pairing tests and add focused coverage for commit, snapshot, and quota behavior. No integration-list registration applies based on the inspected files.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

`MambaHybridCacheManagerV2` gates its context commit path on a blanket `not self.is_draft`
rather than the base class's `_can_publish_block_reuse`. A separate one-model draft KV pool
therefore never publishes into its radix tree and can never be matched: when the target
reuses a prefix of depth `R` it computes only `[R, P)`, so the draft's pages for `[0, R)`
come off the free list still holding an earlier request's contents.

Output is unaffected — every draft token is verified against the target. The cost is
acceptance rate.

The gate the subclass overrides does not apply to this pool: a separate one-model draft pool
is attention-only (`local_num_mamba_layers == 0`), so it has no recurrent state and
`request.expect_snapshot_points` is target geometry.

### Changes

- `try_commit_blocks` / `update_context_resources`: route a draft-role pool to the base
  class's commit path.
- `_supports_draft_reuse_match_backoff`: pool-role-aware counterpart to
  `_supports_reuse_match_backoff`, since a draft pool holds only the speculation layers.
  Defaults `True` on `KVCacheManagerV2`, so it is a no-op except for
  `MambaHybridCacheManagerV2` (opts in) and `DeepseekV4CacheManager` /
  `QSAMambaHybridCacheManagerV2` (opt out — QSA's draft pool adds a `Role.INDEX_KEY` buffer
  and a `QSA_INDEX_POSITION` page, which the attention-only argument does not cover).
- `_drop_advisory_draft_lookahead`: waive the advisory lookahead trim on a paired draft pool.
  The scheduler caps the target at the draft's claim and the target *is* the recurrent pool,
  so a one-token trim costs a whole snapshot interval (639 → 576, 63 → 0). Exact
  verification already rejects a bad draft token; relaxed acceptance does not verify exactly
  and keeps the trim.
- `_joint_reuse_supported`: consult the draft-pool attribute.

### Results

Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, MTP + block reuse, snapshot interval 64. Acceptance length,
7 paired runs per workload:

| Workload | Before | After | Delta | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| qmsum warm (~6.7k prompt, ~99% reused) | 2.3541 | 2.4390 | +0.085 tok (+3.61%) | 0.0025 |
| qmsum cold (control) | 2.5976 | 2.5777 | −0.020 tok (−0.77%) | 0.45 |
| GSM8K n=32 | 3.4991 | 3.5550 | +0.056 tok (+1.60%) | 0.034 |

Max AL is 4. The cold arm is the null control and does not move, as expected: cold requests
populate rather than reuse. At GSM8K n=1319 the draft's pages are recycled from other
requests rather than unwritten, and AL is flat (3.465 → 3.454).

Eval time is unaffected within noise: GSM8K n=1319 81.2s → 82.4s, with target reuse
bit-identical to baseline at 0.8501 / 26,090 blocks. Without the lookahead waiver the same
run costs 0.7643 / 23,454 blocks and +12.4%.

title: [#19485][bugfix] Prevent OOB index in vanilla top-p sampling
body:
## Description

Fix vanilla top-p sampling when fp32 cumulative probability remains below a valid near-1 `top_p` threshold.

In this case, `torch.searchsorted` can return `vocab_size`, which is outside the valid vocabulary index range. The subsequent `scatter_` then accesses that out-of-bounds index and can trigger a CUDA device-side assert.

Closes #19485

## Changes

- Clamp the `torch.searchsorted` result to the valid vocabulary index range before the subsequent scatter.
- Preserve existing behavior when the cumulative probability crosses `top_p`.
- Preserve the full probability distribution when fp32 accumulation does not reach a near-1 `top_p` threshold.
- Add regression coverage for:
  - near-1 `top_p` values where no threshold crossing occurs,
  - mixed batches containing crossing and non-crossing rows,
  - ordinary nucleus-sampling values (`0.9`, `0.95`, `0.999`).

## Validation

- Reproduced the original near-1 `top_p` failure condition, including the out-of-bounds index (`vocab_size`) that causes the scatter failure.
- Verified the fixed implementation on NVIDIA Tesla T4 (SM75) with CUDA.
- Verified the exact near-1 reproduction no longer triggers the device-side assert.
- Verified mixed crossing/no-crossing batches.
- Verified seeded deterministic behavior.
- Verified ordinary `top_p` values (`0.9`, `0.95`, `0.999`) against an independent nucleus-sampling reference.
- Verified `top_p=1.0`, top-k interaction, and relevant boundary/edge cases.
- Verified outputs remain bit-identical for cases where the original implementation was already valid.
- `git diff --check` passes.

### Test Environment

- NVIDIA Tesla T4 (SM75)
- NVIDIA PyTorch 26.02 container
- PyTorch 2.11.0a0+nv26.02
- TensorRT-LLM commit `7edb2b2a18`

### Pytest Status

Targeted repository pytest collection is blocked in the T4 environment by missing `mpi4py` and additional native/dependency requirements. TensorRT-LLM native extensions are unavailable in this environment, and SM75 is not a supported native build architecture for this checkout.

The regression behavior was therefore validated independently on CPU and CUDA, including the exact failure condition and the post-fix behavior.

## Issue

Closes #19485
---
Requesting review from @karljang, @cascade812, and @tongyuantongyu. Thank you for your time and review!

title: [None][perf] Publish MoE all-to-all counters before the dispatch data issue
body:
## Summary

Two related changes to the MoE all-to-all CFT (counted-write) path:

1. **Publish the receive counters before the dispatch data issue.** `send_counters` is
   final once every CTA has routed, so the elected CTA can publish `recv_counters` to its
   peers at that point rather than after the data issue. Peers then see the counts while the
   transfer is still in flight, and the only work left after the issue is polling for them.
   The election and publish move into `cft_elect_and_publish` / `cft_publish_recv_counters`
   so both the zero-token fast path and the routing path share them.

   The completion-flag wait budget also becomes `TLLM_MOE_A2A_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, since
   multi-rank warmup can enter these kernels with large rank skew while peers are still
   JIT-compiling.

2. **Make the CFT path reachable via `TRTLLM_MOE_A2A_FORCE_CFT`.** No caller passes
   `can_use_cft_counted_writes=True`, so without an opt-in the CFT path cannot be exercised
   at all. `TRTLLM_MOE_A2A_FORCE_CFT=1` enables it; `=0` forces it off; leaving the variable
   unset keeps the current behaviour, which is **disabled**.

## Changes

| File | |
|---|---|
| `cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/communicationKernels/moeAlltoAllKernels.cu` | counter publishing, shared elect/publish helpers, timeout budget |
| `cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/communicationKernels/moeAlltoAllKernels.h` | signatures for the above |
| `tensorrt_llm/_torch/moe/fused_moe/communication/moe_alltoall.py` | `TRTLLM_MOE_A2A_FORCE_CFT` opt-in |
| `tensorrt_llm/_torch/moe/fused_moe/communication/nvlink_one_sided.py` | `TRTLLM_MOE_A2A_FORCE_CFT` opt-in |

Builds on #17647, which added the CFT counted-write path.

## Note on the merge with main

An earlier revision of this branch changed the CFT endpoint exchange in
`moeAlltoAllOp.cpp` from `MpiComm::world()` to `MpiComm::session()`. #18300 since reworked
the same code to run without MPI, keeping the exchange world-scoped and documenting why a
session-scoped barrier is unsafe there (a session can be a narrower communicator than
world, so a rank could be released before every peer has imported its endpoints). That
revision is dropped in favour of #18300's version, which also covers the non-MPI path the
original change was reaching for. The commit message of the first commit still mentions the
`session()` change; it is not part of this diff.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/test_moe_a2a_cft.py`
- `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/multi_gpu/test_moe_a2a.py`

CFT requires an NVLink fabric and a driver exporting the CUDA logical-endpoint API.
With the variable unset, the fence path is unchanged and is what CI exercises.

Two test-side changes are included because `test_moe_a2a.py` could not exercise CFT at
all without them:

- The dispatch and combine completion-flag assertions now run only when the counted-write
  path did not. CFT is fence-free and signals through its own counters, so those flags are
  never set when it engages and the unconditional assertion failed every CFT run.
- Dispatch now snapshots the counted-write counters before the transfer and asserts each
  peer advanced by at least the payload bytes implied by its received token count, so a
  silent fallback to the fence path cannot pass as a CFT run.

Verified on an EP8 two-node NVLink configuration with a logical-endpoint-capable driver:
the fence case and both aligned CFT cases pass, and the per-peer counter deltas are
non-zero for every peer and zero for self, confirming counted writes are the transport.

## PR Checklist

- [x] PR title is in `[JIRA/NVBUG/None][type] Summary` format
- [x] Commits are signed off (DCO)
- [x] Tested on CFT-capable hardware; fence-path behaviour is unchanged by default

title: [None][feat] Add skip_rope_quantization switch to NVFP4 cold-page quantization
body:
## Summary

  For every token and KV head, the KV cache holds one K vector and one V vector. In some models only part of the K vector carries the token's position (the RoPE part); the rest does not (the NoPE part). This PR adds one switch to NVFP4 cold-page compression that decides what happens to the RoPE part when a page is compressed:

  `ColdPageQuantizationCompressionConfig.skip_rope_quantization = False`

  * **False (default):** the whole K vector and the whole V vector become NVFP4. Highest compression ratio.
  * **True:** only the NoPE part of the K vector becomes NVFP4. The RoPE part is copied into the cold page unchanged, so it keeps the hot cache's precision (FP8 or BF16). The V vector still becomes NVFP4 in full. A little more accuracy for a lower
  compression ratio.

  The switch is validated for DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5 (`glm_moe_dsa`), and the Qwen3.5 series (`_KEEP_ROPE_PRECISION_MODEL_TYPES`). Any other model type logs one warning and keeps quantizing whole vectors. Draft-model KV caches (speculative decoding)
  always quantize whole vectors, because the codec only holds the target model's config. Adding a model means checking its accuracy and adding its `model_type` to that list.

  Behavior change for DeepSeek-V4: its compressed rows previously always kept the 64 RoPE numbers unchanged. They now follow the switch, so the default quantizes the whole 512-number row (288 B instead of 316 B per FP8 row). The layout used for
  the validated DeepSeek-V4 runs is `keep_rope_precision: true`; the example doc says so.

  ## Design

  * **Kernel:** each hot row (one K or V vector, `raw_row_stride_elements` apart) has one contiguous range that becomes NVFP4, described as `(quantized_range_start, quantized_range_elements)`. Everything before and after the range is copied
  byte-for-byte. This replaces the old "quantized prefix + copied suffix" rule, which could not express Qwen3.5 rows where the RoPE part sits at the start of the vector. The integer metadata table stays 7 columns and the nanobind launcher
  signature is unchanged.
  * **Codec (`nvfp4_quantization.py`):** one helper, `_calculate_quantized_range`, returns the range for a row. With the switch off it is the whole row. With it on, the RoPE width comes from `RopeParams.from_config(text_config).dim`, the same
  source the attention layers use; key-only layers are MLA latent vectors (RoPE at the end, checked against `kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim == head_dim`), K/V layers rotate the leading numbers, and DeepSeek-V4 compressed rows are 448 NoPE + 64
  RoPE. Rows that are entirely RoPE, RoPE in the middle of a vector, or a range not aligned to 16-element scale groups are rejected.
  * **Docs:** feature page, example page, and developer guide describe the switch in terms of K/V vectors, NoPE and RoPE; the DeepSeek-V4 support-table rows and section are updated for the new default.

  ## Bytes per hot row at FP8 (V is always NVFP4)

  | Row | `keep_rope_precision` off | `keep_rope_precision` on |
  |---|---|---|
  | MLA latent 576 | 324 B (1.78x) | 352 B (1.64x) |
  | DeepSeek-V4 compressed 512 | 288 B (1.78x) | 316 B (1.62x) |
  | Qwen3.5 K 256 + V 256 | 288 B (1.78x) | 316 B (1.62x) |

title: [None][fix] Drain guided-decoder host functions before GIL-holding forward calls
body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/guided_decoder.py`: `CapturableGuidedDecoder` now waits on `bitmask_event` as the last step of `execute`, `execute_draft_batch` and `rollback_rejected_batch`, so the CUDA host functions that build the bitmask have finished before control returns to the caller. The wait is skipped while a CUDA graph is being captured. `Event.synchronize` releases the GIL, which is what lets the pending host-function callbacks run.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/speculative/interface.py`: the `SpecWorkerBase` guided-decoder helper routes through the draining entry points, including the skip-drafting path.
- Behavior change: host-side ordering only. The bitmask consumer was already ordered against the same event on the device, so decode results are unchanged. Fixes a rank-wide deadlock (host function waiting for the GIL while a GIL-holding native forward triggers a context-synchronizing lazy kernel load) that CUDA-graph warmup with a one-engine drafter hit deterministically.

## QA Engineer Review

- New CPU-only unit test `tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/hw_agnostic/test_guided_hostfunc_drain.py` (198 lines): asserts each enqueue site drains as its last step, that the drain is skipped under CUDA-graph capture and for the non-capturable decoder, and that the `SpecWorkerBase` helper still executes the decoder on both the drafting and skip-drafting paths.
- No GPU test added: the deadlock needs a multi-rank one-engine drafter with a cold kernel cache, which the L0 unit stages cannot reproduce. Validated manually on the 4-rank warmup that originally wedged.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

`CapturableGuidedDecoder` builds its bitmask from CUDA host functions, and each is a callback into Python that must take the GIL. A one-engine drafter (e.g. DFlash) runs a draft forward right after guided execution, and that forward enters native extension calls that hold the GIL for their whole duration (`flash_attn_with_kvcache`); when such a call triggers CUDA lazy kernel-module loading, the driver performs a context-synchronizing operation. A guided-decoder host function still pending at that point deadlocks the rank: the device is parked at the host-function node, the callback waits for the GIL, and the GIL holder waits for the device. Peer ranks then spin in NCCL, wedging the whole server with no error and no further log line. CUDA-graph warmup hits this deterministically at the first warmup shape whose kernel instantiation is not yet loaded (gdb evidence: pending `cudaHostFuncTrampoline` threads on 3/4 ranks, main threads in `cudaFuncSetAttribute` -> `cuKernelGetFunction`).

The existing `set_stance("force_eager")` mitigation (pytorch#163061) covers only torch.compile kernels, not a plain extension call.

Fix: drain at the enqueue sites. `CapturableGuidedDecoder` waits on `bitmask_event` (recorded on the side stream after every host function) as the last step of `execute`, `execute_draft_batch` and `rollback_rejected_batch`, skipped while a CUDA graph is being captured (host waits are illegal there, and captured host nodes do not run until replay). `Event.synchronize` releases the GIL, which is exactly what lets the pending callbacks run. Host-side ordering only; the bitmask consumer is already ordered against the same event on the device, so results are unchanged, and no caller discipline is required.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/hw_agnostic/test_guided_hostfunc_drain.py` (CPU-only): asserts each enqueue site drains as its last step, that the drain is skipped under CUDA-graph capture and for the non-capturable decoder, and that the `SpecWorkerBase` helper still executes the decoder (including the skip-drafting path).

## PR Checklist

Please review the following before submitting your PR:
- PR description clearly explains what and why. If using CodeRabbit's summary, please make sure it makes sense.
- PR Follows [TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of your knowledge.
- Test cases are provided for new code paths (see [test instructions](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/tests#1-how-does-the-ci-work))
- If PR introduces API changes, an appropriate PR label is added - either `api-compatible` or `api-breaking`. For `api-breaking`, include `BREAKING` in the PR title.
- Any new dependencies have been scanned for license and vulnerabilities
- [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) updated if ownership changes
- Documentation updated as needed
- Update [tava architecture diagram](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/tava_architecture_diagram.md) if there is a significant design change in PR.

title: [https://nvbugs/6812347][fix] Do not pass expert-count args to the Rubin MoE finalize op
body:
## Description

On Rubin, every CuteDSL NVFP4 fused-finalize MoE path fails at warmup:

```
RuntimeError: Unknown keyword argument 'expert_counts' for operator
'trtllm::cute_dsl_nvfp4_grouped_gemm_finalize_inplace_rubin'.
```

The call site picks between the Rubin and Blackwell finalize ops, then calls the
winner with a fixed kwarg list. #16919 added `expert_counts`/`expert_capacity` to
that list and to the Blackwell op, but the Rubin op never declared them.

`can_use_deep_ep_direct_metadata()` already excludes SM107, so Rubin only ever
passed `None`/`0` — the call failed purely because the names are absent from the
schema. That broke plain TP/EP/PP and static-EPLB too, not just DeepEP.

## Fix

Pass the two args only on the Blackwell path, and raise `NotImplementedError` if
count-native metadata ever reaches Rubin, so the SM107 exclusion fails loudly
instead of silently. One file, +19/-5, no kernel changes.

## Test Coverage

VR200 (SM107), 8x GPU, `1.3.0rc28.dev202609210001` wheel patched in place so
before/after use identical binaries:

- `TestNemotronV3Super::test_nvfp4_4gpus_static_eplb[moe_backend=CUTEDSL]`: 12 errors before, 0 after
- `TestGLM52NVFP4::test_tep[tp_size=8-ep_size=8]` (the bug's repro): **PASSED**, GSM8K 94.31 vs 90.0 reference

#16919's only test-list change was `l0_b200.yml`, so no Rubin job covered this
call site — worth adding one.

## Related

Fixes https://nvbugs/6812347 · Introduced by #16919 (`c2cec526a`)

title: [None][chore] Add per-rank routing/scheduling observability to the iteration log
body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Adds scheduling counters for attention-DP dummy and unscheduled requests in both scheduling paths.
- The diff also reformats many imports in `py_executor.py`, which increases review scope without an indicated behavior change.
- No public API changes are shown. Review findings and test results are unavailable.

## QA Engineer Review

No test changes.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/py_executor.py`: Verify counter initialization and updates in both scheduling paths. Confirm that dummy counts use `scheduled_batch.all_requests()` and unscheduled counts equal active requests minus the scheduled batch size.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Diagnosing attention-DP load imbalance today requires reconstructing state from per-request perf metrics. This PR adds per-rank routing and scheduling fields to the existing `print_iter_log` iteration line. It is log-only and touches a single file (`py_executor.py`).

**Per-rank fields on the iteration line:**

```
..., states = {...}, num_active = 14, num_fetched = 3, num_dummy = 1, num_unscheduled = 5
```

- `num_active` — `len(active_requests)` at the iteration boundary (top of the loop, after the previous iteration's completions were removed and before the next fetch).
- `num_fetched` — new requests the ADP router assigned to this rank during this iteration (delta of the cumulative fetch counter, tracked in the logging closure).
- `num_dummy` — attention-DP pad dummies in this iteration's scheduled batch (0/1 per rank, padded in when the rank would otherwise run an empty batch). `num_scheduled_requests` already counts the pad, so subtract `num_dummy` to recover the real scheduled count.
- `num_unscheduled` — active requests **not** placed in this iteration's batch (`len(active_requests) − scheduled batch_size`). Sampled at schedule time, so the pad cancels in both terms and it never mixes epochs the way `active − num_scheduled` would (the `num_scheduled_requests` printed on this line is the previous iteration's).

`num_dummy` and `num_unscheduled` are captured where `num_scheduled_requests` is already set (both executor-loop variants), and therefore lag one iteration behind `num_active` / `num_fetched`, consistent with `num_scheduled_requests`.

title: [None][infra] Enforce copyright headers via pre-commit hook; make CodeRabbit a backstop
body:
## Problem

CodeRabbit posts recurring "add a copyright header" / "update the copyright year" comments on PRs that touch or add files without headers. The policy (CODING_GUIDELINES.md "NVIDIA Copyright", AGENTS.md) is real, but nothing enforces it mechanically, and ~770 pre-existing source files have no header — so the same nuisance comments reappear on every PR that touches them.

## Change

**1. New `copyright-header` pre-commit hook** (`scripts/check_copyright_header.py`):

- Inserts the SPDX-style NVIDIA Apache-2.0 header on newly added source files (`.py/.c/.cc/.cpp/.cxx/.h/.hpp/.cu/.cuh`), after any shebang/coding line. Idempotent.
- Bumps the NVIDIA copyright year on modified files (`2022-2023` → `2022-2026`, style-preserving). The year check applies only to files with uncommitted changes, so post-merge CI running `pre-commit --all-files` on a clean checkout stays green. `--assume-modified` overrides this for manual repair runs on already-committed trees.
- Header *detection* is lenient: all historical NVIDIA header variants pass (classic `(c)` blocks, SPDX style, bare `Copyright NNNN NVIDIA`), and any non-NVIDIA copyright header also passes — TensorRT-LLM contributions are DCO-based with no CLA, so external contributors retain their own copyright and may use their own copyright line. The NVIDIA header is only the insertion default.

**2. Two committed lists, deliberately separate:**

- `scripts/copyright_header_excludes.txt` — **permanent** exclusions: third-party/vendored/generated code that must never receive an NVIDIA header (vendored `triton_kernels/`, sha256, generated cubin artifacts, and three vLLM-derived files that keep the upstream "contributors to the vLLM project" notice). The hook refuses to run if this file is missing.
- `scripts/copyright_header_baseline.txt` — 772 grandfathered pre-existing files with no header, expected to shrink via backfill. Regenerate with `--update-baseline`.

Empty files (e.g. bare `__init__.py`, 53 of them) are exempt.

**3. CodeRabbit becomes a backstop, not a nag** (`.coderabbit.yaml`): a global instruction tells it to stay silent for exempt files (excludes list, baseline, out-of-scope/empty files, non-NVIDIA-authored headers), and when a header/year issue in an in-scope file indicates the hook didn't run, to post a single "pre-commit hooks appear not installed" warning with the repair command instead of per-file header comments.

## Testing

- Full tree (`4521` source files) passes the hook on a clean checkout, both directly and via `pre-commit run copyright-header --all-files` (post-merge CI mode).
- Verified: header insertion on new `.py` (shebang preserved, `py_compile` clean) and `.cpp` files; idempotency; stale-year detection fires only on modified files and `--fix` rewrites `2022-2023, NVIDIA` → `2022-2026, NVIDIA` in place; external-contributor header (non-NVIDIA copyright + SPDX tag) accepted; hook hard-fails if the excludes file is deleted.

## Open questions for reviewers

1. **Header format**: CODING_GUIDELINES.md still shows the classic `Copyright (c) 2025, NVIDIA CORPORATION` block, while newer infra files (and this hook's insertion) use the SPDX form. Should CODING_GUIDELINES.md be updated to the SPDX form?
2. **External contributions**: with DCO and no CLA, contributors keep their copyright, so the hook accepts any copyright header rather than demanding the NVIDIA one. Does this match the intended policy, or should new files from external contributors also carry the NVIDIA header (which would need legal review)?
3. **Baseline backfill**: stamping headers onto the 772 baseline files needs a provenance pass first (some are adapted from HF/DeepSeek code). Proposal: per-directory backfill PRs, each reviewed for third-party origin, moving genuinely third-party files to the permanent excludes list.
4. **Pre-merge CI**: the year check currently enforces at local commit time only. It could be extended to pre-merge CI by passing `--assume-modified` for the changed-file list in `scripts/release_check.py`.
5. A handful of files carry unparsable copyright lines (e.g. `Copyright (out) 1993-2026` typos in `cpp/tensorrt_llm/thop/`); the hook skips the year check there. Worth fixing separately.
