title: [https://nvbugs/6708299][fix] Support group_size=32 for W4A16_NVFP4 and validate NVFP4 group sizes
body:
## Description

ModelOpt's Qwen3.5-27B `nvfp4_mlp_weight_only` checkpoint declares 32-element scale groups. The loader assumed 16 and allocated twice as many scales, failing with 5,570,560 versus 2,785,280 elements (NVBug 6708299).

Support 16/32-element groups in dense W4A16_NVFP4 Linear allocation, checkpoint loading, ROW-TP sharding, and Triton dequantization. W4A4 and Marlin remain 16-only. The shared width resolver now lives in `quantization/utils/fp4_utils.py`: omitted/None widths resolve to 16, while explicit unsupported values, including 128, are consistently rejected by ModelOpt parsing and Linear construction. The implicit AWQ/GPTQ default remains compatible without silently accepting an explicitly declared 128.

Review follow-up:
- Restrict the MoE guard to NVFP4/NVFP4_ARC/W4A16_NVFP4. Preserve W4A8_NVFP4_FP8's backend-fixed 32-element allocation, fixing the four B200 failures from CI run 60308.
- Reject 32-element W4A16 expert entries during ModelOpt parsing and Qwen normalization before backend selection/promotion. The reported 27B checkpoint is dense and has no MoE experts; this PR does not add 32-element W4A16 MoE support. Rename the supported-width constant to explicitly identify dense Linear support.
- Send 32-element Qwen LM heads through the existing load-time bf16 dequantization fallback, avoiding full LM-head dequantization on every decode step. Native 16-element quantized LM-head paths remain enabled.
- Keep direct quant_config access and repair the older Marlin test fixtures to match real Linear modules.
- Mark hardware-independent cases cpu_only. The CPU list already covers the MoE, modules, and modeling directories; the linear file is already listed for H100/GB10 GPU coverage. Remove explicit H100 entries for the two Qwen tests now covered by CPU CI.

## Test Coverage

Validated from an isolated checkout/container on one B200, using PyTorch 2.14.0a0 (DLFW 26.08) with compatible 1.3.0rc26 native binaries:

- **109 passed** across `test_hf_quant_config.py`, `test_w4a16_nvfp4_linear.py`, `test_nvfp4_moe_block_width.py`, and `test_modeling_qwen3_5_vl.py` (`-k "not test_all"`). Includes actual 16/32-group GPU dequantization, ROW-TP scale sharding, and Qwen construction/weight-loading smoke coverage.

title: [None][perf] Avoid prefix probes when the KV cache v2 context chunk budget is insufficient
body:
## Description

With chunked prefill and prefix-aware scheduling enabled, the KV cache v2 scheduler probes pending context requests even when the remaining token budget guarantees that their admission will be skipped. Long prefixes and many pending requests can make these unnecessary probes expensive.

Check the existing chunk-budget eligibility predicate before the per-request prefix probe, and share that predicate with chunked admission. Continue scanning so encoder requests can still schedule. Preserve unlimited-budget behavior, the minimum chunk-unit requirement for FCFS, and positive sub-unit budgets for FORCE_CHUNK. Nonchunked admission is unchanged.

An internal benchmark measured approximately 12% higher token throughput with this change on the evaluated workload.

## Test Coverage

Add nine synthetic CPU test cases in `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_v2_scheduler.py`, covering:

- Exhausted and sub-unit budgets after a context chunk: one prefix probe instead of twenty.
- Generation consuming the entire budget before context admission.
- Encoder admission despite insufficient context chunk budget.
- FORCE_CHUNK admission at a snapshot boundary shorter than the chunk unit.
- Unlimited budgets under both chunking policies.
- A budget-only skip preserving an existing context claim and cursor without probing, preparing, freeing, or suspending it.

The existing `unittest/_torch/executor` entry in `l0_cpu.yml` includes this CPU-marked test file.

Validation on the proposed upstream patch:

- Ruff lint and formatting, Python syntax, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- The extracted budget predicate matched the previous inline logic across 2,088 combinations of remaining budget, chunk unit, and policy.
- The scheduler suite could not collect locally because PyTorch is unavailable. Run `python3 -m pytest tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_v2_scheduler.py -q` in a configured TensorRT-LLM environment before submission.
- Prior internal validation: the original six regression cases failed before the fix and the patched scheduler suite passed 226 tests. Those results do not validate this public-main checkout or the three additional cases.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Complete upstream scheduler runtime validation and reviewer checks before submission.

title: [#18609][fix] Do not require encoder tokens for cross prefix reuse
body:
Fixes #18609.

### Problem

Every generation request against `openai/whisper-large-v3` on the PyTorch backend dies in the C++ capacity scheduler, before the forward pass:

```
File ".../scheduler/scheduler.py", line 462, in schedule_request
    return self.impl(
RuntimeError: bad optional access
```

`capacityScheduler.cpp` dereferences the encoder unique tokens at three places, guarded only by the presence of a cross KV cache manager with block reuse on:

```cpp
auto uniqueTokens = *(req->getEncoderUniqueTokens().value());
```

None of the three checks whether the optional holds anything.

### Why it is empty

`mEncoderUniqueTokens` is derived from encoder **tokens** alone (`llmRequest.h:2272`):

```cpp
if (mEncoderTokens.has_value() && mEncoderTokens.value())
{
    ...
    mEncoderUniqueTokens = encoderUniqueTokens;
}
```

Whisper's encoder input is features, not tokens: `modeling_whisper.py:788` passes `"encoder_input_features"`, and `llm_request.py:928-934` leaves `encoder_input_tokens` as `None`. So the optional is never populated.

`enable_block_reuse` defaults to `True` (`llm_args.py:4106`), and an encoder-decoder run must set `cross_kv_cache_fraction`, which is what creates the cross manager. Both guard conditions therefore hold on a default run, which is why the reporter saw it on every request. It is not architecture-specific; the reporter's SM120 box is not what selects this path.

### Change

Add the missing condition at each of the three sites.

Prefix reuse matches on token prefixes, so a features-based encoder has nothing for `analyzePrefixReuse` to walk. Leaving `crossSummary` unset is the state its two consumers already handle:

```cpp
// oneManagerBeneficialToSkip
return summary.has_value() && summary->firstNewBlock.has_value() && ...

// registerContributedBlocks
if (crossSummary.has_value() && crossSummary->firstNewBlock.has_value()) { ... }
```

and it is the state they already see whenever there is no cross manager, block reuse is off, or the manager is variable-window.

The same header already distinguishes the two shapes of encoder input, which is what made the token-only assumption visible (`llmRequest.h:663`):

```cpp
/// @return Encoder input length, or nullopt when this request has no encoder side.
[[nodiscard]] std::optional<SizeType32> tryGetEncoderInputLen() const
{
    if (mEncoderInputFeatures.has_value()) { ... }
    if (getEncoderTokens().has_value())    { ... }
    return std::nullopt;
}
```

### Verification

- `clang-format` 16.0.0, the version pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, reports no diff on the file.
- `grep` finds three dereferences of `getEncoderUniqueTokens().value()` in this file; all three now sit behind `has_value()`.

### What I have not done

I did not reproduce the failure or run this patch myself. I have no SM120 GPU and no Whisper setup; the analysis is from reading `main`, and the reporter's trace is what located it.

**Since writing that, @ravo42-maker has run it.** They applied this hunk onto the `v1.3.0rc25` tag (785c948, where all three sites are identical), built a wheel for `120-real`, and ran `openai/whisper-large-v3` on an RTX 5070 Ti. With `max_input_len=1500` and block reuse left on, stock rc25 raises `bad optional access` and rc25 + this change transcribes the clip in 3.95 s. Their five-run table isolates block reuse as the only variable between the crash and a working run. See the comment below; the verification is theirs, not mine.

I also have not added a regression test. The natural one is a capacity-scheduler unit test with a request carrying encoder input features and no encoder tokens, with a cross manager and block reuse enabled. I would rather add it in the shape this repository prefers than guess, so please say if you want it here.

### Note beyond this fix

The reporter lists four further gaps in the same issue: no `/v1/audio/transcriptions` route, no Whisper chat template shipped, no Whisper example or test in the container, and no release that currently provides a working Whisper path. This change addresses only the scheduler crash.

title: [None][feat] Support attention DP in V2 KV cache connectors
body:
Extend the V2 KV Cache Connector to support attention data parallelism (ADP).

The existing implementation assumes attention tensor parallelism (TP), where all ranks process the same requests and maintain corresponding prefix-cache state. Rank 0 runs the connector scheduler and broadcasts its decisions, while each rank’s worker transfers its local KV-cache shards.

With ADP, ranks process different requests and maintain independent prefix trees, so request-level coordination through a single scheduler no longer applies. This PR gives each ADP rank its own connector scheduler adapter and worker. Request metadata, allocation feedback, and transfer completion remain local to the owning rank, while adapters can share a common external cache pool.

Gemma4Attention registers itself into the inner ModelConfig.extra_attrs that is passed to Gemma4ForCausalLM, but PyTorchModelEngine.model_forward publishes the outer wrapper's model_config.extra_attrs to the thread-local before running the model. The two are different objects, so attn_layers never reaches the thread-local and extract_extra_attrs asserts "Attention layer is not registered".

Eager execution is unaffected because the custom inplace attention op is gated on is_torch_compiling() or is_in_breakable_cuda_graph(), so the lookup only runs under CUDA graph capture. The visible symptom is that both prefill_cuda_graph_backend=piecewise and =breakable fail to initialize on Gemma4.

Propagating the inner config's extra_attrs to the outer one after the decoder is constructed fixes both paths.

Measured on gemma-4-E4B-it (BF16, TP1, 1x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, SM120) with prefill_cuda_graph_backend=breakable, ISL 25 / OSL 5:

  concurrency 1: TTFT 48.3 -> 14.5 ms, request latency 83.0 -> 50.5 ms,
                 throughput 11.9 -> 19.4 req/s
  concurrency 4: TTFT 93.3 -> 23.2 ms, request latency 129.8 -> 61.3 ms,
                 throughput 30.2 -> 63.5 req/s

title: [TRTLLMINF-336][infra] Enable BOLT postmerge consume
body:
Pass boltPublishCanonical=true from the postmerge pipeline's BOLT-Profile-Gen launch, so the tarball that run re-BOLTs is pushed back to its artifactPath under the canonical name and the un-BOLTed original is preserved as unbolted-<tarball>. Canonical now means BOLTed for the postmerge build, matching what premerge consume already does to the premerge build (Build.groovy's applyLatestBolt) and what the overlay does to published images.

The scaffolding landed in 0beff32139 with the toggle off. publishBoltedCanonical, the unbolted- snapshot, the idempotent re-run handling, and the boltPublishCanonical parameter are all already in place, so this only changes the answer to "should this run republish a canonical".

The helper still requires applyProfiles=true and promote=true, both of which only the postmerge launch sets: an on-demand or premerge generate-and-consume run (promote=false) publishes nothing even with the toggle on. applyProfiles is passed explicitly here rather than left to its default, since publishing silently does nothing without the merge job's BOLT_APPLY=1 step.

In-run effect: the SBSA test stages sequenced after BOLT-Profile-Gen pull the canonical tarball from this same artifactPath, so postmerge tests now exercise the BOLTed build -- test coverage on the very bundle the run promotes for premerge to consume. Scoped to aarch64/SBSA, the only triple the producer profiles; TensorRT-LLM.tar.gz is untouched. The stage stays best-effort under the existing catchError(buildResult: 'SUCCESS'), so a failed publish leaves the canonical un-BOLTed instead of failing postmerge.

Also reports the previously silent skip when the toggle is on but a precondition is unmet, a path only reachable once postmerge sets it.

Rollback: drop boltPublishCanonical from the launch, or set the job parameter to false. Already-published canonicals are recoverable from unbolted-<tarball>.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- `BoltProfileGen` publishes `bolted-<tarball>` only when `boltPublishBolted`, `applyProfiles`, and `promote` are all `"true"`.
- Profiling uses the canonical input to prevent double-BOLTing on reruns.
- `L0_MergeRequest` marks profile-generation failures as `UNSTABLE` and continues downstream tests.
- `L0_Test` retries Artifactory probes and falls back to the canonical artifact when the BOLTed artifact is unavailable.
- Review finding counts are unavailable. The supplied CI result reports a successful `PR_Github` job and a failed downstream `L0_MergeRequest_PR` pipeline.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Two small hardening fixes for multimodal media input handling:

1. **Reject data URIs whose declared MIME type mismatches the content part modality.** A data URI in an `image_url` (or audio/video) content part was decoded even when its declared media type said something else entirely (`text/plain`, `application/pdf`, ...): the per-modality loaders sniffed the payload bytes and ignored the declared type. Silently decoding mislabeled payloads hides client bugs and diverges from reference OpenAI-compatible servers, which return 400. Now each media IO class declares its expected MIME prefix (`image/`, `audio/`, `video/`) and `BaseMediaIO.async_load` validates the declared type before dispatching to `load_base64`. Data URIs that omit the media type are still accepted for backward compatibility.

2. **`TRTLLM_MEDIA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=1` opt-in for media URLs resolving to private addresses.** Media URL validation requires resolved IPs to be global, so every internal or loopback http(s) media URL is rejected with no opt-out. That is the right SSRF default for internet-facing servers, but it blocks legitimate airgapped and intranet deployments, forcing `file://` workarounds. The new env var skips only the non-global-address rejection; default OFF, so the SSRF posture is unchanged unless the operator sets it. Scheme, hostname, and multicast checks still apply, the opt-in covers redirect hops through the same validator, and enabling it logs a one-time warning. The rejection message now names the variable so operators can find the switch.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/inputs/test_async_media_loading.py`: data-URI MIME reject/accept/missing-MIME cases for image, audio, and video.
- `tests/unittest/inputs/test_url_validation.py`: the opt-in admits private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT addresses (including redirect targets); default and non-"1" values still reject; multicast and non-http(s) schemes rejected either way.

title: [None][fix] Share speculative capture buffers across CUDA graph buckets
body:
## Description

`DFlashSpecMetadata`/`DSparkSpecMetadata` allocate a hidden-state capture buffer sized for the full token budget (`max_num_tokens x hidden_size * num_capture_layers`). `create_cuda_graph_metadata()` shallow-copies the metadata and re-runs `__post_init__` for every CUDA graph bucket, so each bucket allocated its own full-size buffer even though model forwards and their consumers are ordered on the same execution stream and never need more than one.

This change keeps the existing buffer when it is already compatible (same shape, dtype and device) and reallocates only on a real mismatch, so all graph buckets share one full-token-budget scratch buffer. Behavior is unchanged; per-bucket memory for the capture buffer drops to a single allocation.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/hw_agnostic/test_capture_buffer.py` (cpu_only): buckets share the parent buffer, incompatible buffers (rows/width/dtype/device/missing) are reallocated, no-capture configurations stay `None`.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/test_capture_buffer_cuda.py` (CUDA): graph capture/replay across alternating buckets writes through the shared buffer and replays correctly, including after the parent metadata is garbage-collected; multi-device allocation follows the current device.

title: [None][feat] agent-flow: backend-independent tools and required-tool policy
body:
## Summary

Brings the Codex backend to parity with Claude Code in `agent-flow`, and moves the
pieces that both backends need out of the Claude-specific path.

### Backend-independent tools

Tool definition and MCP result conversion now live in a shared `agent_flow/tools.py`,
so both backends consume one definition format (`from agent_flow import tool`).
Python shorthand and `TypedDict` inputs normalize to JSON Schema. Resource links and
embedded text resources become readable tool output, image results retain their MIME
type, and unsupported result types return explicit tool errors rather than appearing
to succeed with missing output. Existing Claude SDK tool objects still work.

### Required-tool policy on either backend

Workflows previously stacked one Claude `Stop` hook per required tool to get AND
semantics. That is replaced by `AgentLayerConfig.required_tools`, which is
backend-agnostic:

```python
config = AgentLayerConfig(
    backend=BackendConfig(kind="codex", model=CODEX_DEFAULT_MODEL, tools=tools),
    required_tools=("append_reviewer_progress", "update_status"),
)
```

`AgentLayer` observes root-agent tool calls, sends **one** corrective turn on the same
session when calls are missing, and raises `RequiredToolCallError` if that bounded
correction still leaves them missing. Subagent calls and calls from prior invocations
do not discharge the requirement. The policy counts attempts, not successful writes —
tool handlers and workflow validation remain responsible for the outputs. Token
accounting sums both turns, while context occupancy stays the final snapshot rather
than being summed. `require_tool_call_stop_hook` remains available as a Claude-native
alternative for existing callers.

### Codex backend split

`backends/codex.py` is split into `codex_config.py`, `codex_events.py`, and
`codex_transport.py`:

- **config** — session options translate into `thread/start.config` and never edit the
  user's Codex configuration. Unsupported options fail at registration instead of being
  silently ignored, which matters most when they describe tool restrictions.
  `extra_mcp_servers` accepts Claude-style STDIO/HTTP form.
- **events** — the pinned app-server protocol maps onto the shared backend events,
  including subagent activity, structured rate limits, and cache-write tokens.
- **transport** — one isolated notification observer over the SDK's public process and
  request APIs, so descendant turns and account events reach the shared event stream.

Native hooks stay backend-specific: Claude accepts its SDK callbacks, while Codex
rejects per-client hook injection because that trust cannot be verified — configure
Codex hooks natively and prefer `required_tools` for workflow progress/status.

### Other changes

- Context-budget inspection no longer sends a `ping` bootstrap turn, so inspection
  never costs a model turn.
- `UsageInfo.estimated_thread_cost_usd` is reported separately from per-turn `cost_usd`
  and rendered in the console usage line.
- The Claude backend drops its unconditional `can_use_tool` approver; it already runs
  with `permission_mode="bypassPermissions"`.

Also included is the previously staged commit pinning `claude-agent-sdk` 0.2.152 and
`openai-codex` 0.154.0 — the adapters here target those pinned versions.

## Test Coverage

New: `tests/test_tools.py`, `tests/test_codex_config.py`, `tests/test_codex_events.py`,
`tests/test_codex_transport.py`, `tests/test_codex_backend.py` (the oversized
`test_backends.py` is split along the same seams), plus required-tool policy coverage in
`tests/test_agent_layer.py` and per-workflow tests.

```
$ python -m pytest tests -q
1300 passed, 3 skipped in 43.40s

$ pre-commit run --files <changed files>
all hooks passed
```

Transport tests run against the pinned SDK, so a future SDK bump that moves the
notification hook fails here rather than silently dropping child turns.

title: [TRTLLMINF-381][fix] classify CI failures from originating step logs
body:
## Background

Jenkins shell-step exceptions often contain only an exit code while the actionable failure signature remains in the originating step console log. The shared libraries now expose policy-neutral originating-step evidence and map evidence query IDs back to the existing TRT-LLM failure catalog.

## Changes

- Collect originating-step evidence at Build and L0 classification boundaries.
- Reuse one evidence result within each retry attempt for result suppression and retry decisions.
- Propagate exhausted infrastructure failures as typed InfraFailure values so infra-scoped fail-fast can defer them without cancelling sibling stages.
- Preserve interruption and user-failure behavior, including SLURM/K8s scope isolation.
- Remove the temporary sbatch_output.txt readback path because sbatch output is already printed into the originating Jenkins step log.
- Preserve the primary stage failure when cleanup or result-upload handling also fails.

This also covers the SLURM bring-up classification gap described by TRTLLMINF-415: bring-up failures are classified at the outer SLURM retry boundary after resource cleanup, then propagated as typed infra failures when local retry is exhausted.

## Dependencies

- bloom-jenkins-shared-lib https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/TensorRT/Infrastructure/bloom-jenkins-shared-lib/-/merge_requests/2700
- trtllm-jenkins-shared-lib  https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/ftp/infra/trtllm-jenkins-shared-lib/-/merge_requests/106

Both shared-library changes are merged.

## Impact

No catalog patterns or retry budgets change. Only failures matching the existing scoped catalog, or failures already thrown as typed infra errors, are retried/deferred. Interruptions and unmatched/user failures continue to propagate as their original exceptions.

## Testing

Local checks:

- /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.12 tests/unittest/tools/test_infra_dry_run_pipeline.py (5 passed)
- pre-commit run --files jenkins/Build.groovy jenkins/L0_Test.groovy (passed)
- git diff --check (passed)

Jenkins validation:

- Run the standard PR CI with /bot run.
- Run InfraDryRun=true to verify the successful K8s and SLURM dispatcher paths remain unchanged.
- Use Jenkins Replay or a temporary validation commit to make an originating shell step print a known scoped catalog signature and exit nonzero while its exception remains only script returned exit code N. Verify the matched signature drives the expected retry, intermediate JUnit is suppressed, exhausted infra propagates as typed InfraFailure, cleanup runs first, and sibling stages continue under infra-scoped fail-fast.
https://prod.blsm.nvidia.com/sw-tensorrt-llm-github-4/blue/organizations/jenkins/LLM%2Fmain%2FL0_Test-x86_64-Single-GPU/detail/L0_Test-x86_64-Single-GPU/2774/pipeline/
- Negative controls: an unmatched test failure must not retry, and a user abort or pipeline timeout must remain a PipelineInterruption and must not be deferred.

The normal InfraDryRun is a success-path regression check; targeted failure injection is required to exercise the new evidence-classification path.

title: [#19362][fix] Name the act fusion in the skip reason
body:
Addresses the second option in #19362.

### Problem

`test_cute_dsl_nvfp4` and `test_cute_dsl_nvfp4_4gpus` skip on anything other than SM 100 or 103 with:

```
CuTe DSL blockscaling mm supports SM 100 and 103 only
```

That reads as though CuTe DSL blockscaling matmul as a whole stops at SM 103. It no longer does: #18761 and #18765 added SM107 CuTe DSL dense GEMM and BMM ops, with their own `*_rubin` test files. What these two tests need and do not have is the NVFP4 GEMM with **fused SwiGLU**, which is gated separately in `cute_dsl_custom_ops.py`:

```
CuteDSL NVFP4 SwiGLU backend requires SM 100 (B200) or SM 103 (B300)
CuteDSL NVFP4 SwiGLU FP4Out requires SM 100 or SM 103
```

Someone reading the skip on an SM107 run is pointed at the wrong thing.

### Change

```diff
-            pytest.skip("CuTe DSL blockscaling mm supports SM 100 and 103 only")
+            pytest.skip(
+                "CuTe DSL NVFP4 GEMM+SwiGLU act fusion supports SM 100 and 103 only"
+            )
```

Two sites, the same string, no behaviour change: the same host states skip, for the same reason, with the reason stated accurately. Both docstrings already describe these tests as "GEMM+SwiGLU fusion for shared experts", so the message now agrees with them.

I kept the message self-describing rather than linking the issue, since the skips in this file reference `https://nvbugs/...` and not GitHub issue numbers.

### Verification

- `grep` finds exactly the two occurrences of the old string in the repository; both are changed.
- `yapf --style pyproject.toml -d` reports no diff on the file.
- The file byte-compiles.

### What this is not

This is the reporting half of #19362. Porting the NVFP4 SwiGLU and FP4Out act-fusion GEMMs to SM107 is the other option there, and it is not this change: #18761 and #18765 added roughly 4,400 lines of SM107-specific kernels and dispatch between them, so that work belongs with whoever owns those kernels. I have not touched any gate.

title: [None][feat] BREAKING: serve: default num_serve_frontends to 8 with single-frontend fallback
body:
## Description

Follow-up to #16523 (`num_serve_frontends`): make the plain `trtllm-serve` subcommand run **8 HTTP frontend processes by default** instead of 1.

### Motivation

At high concurrency a `trtllm-serve` worker is host-bound on its single serving process: one asyncio event loop performs every request `json.loads` + pydantic validation and every SSE chunk write. #16523 measured `gen_preprocessing` p50 54 ms @ c512 → 109 ms @ c1024 → 1520 ms @ c2048 on a DSv4 disagg GEN worker while decode step time stayed flat; running several frontends behind one `SO_REUSEPORT` port removes that ceiling. The knob has been the production setting in our agentic disagg configs (8 on CTX, 4 on GEN) since then; this PR makes users get the benefit without knowing the flag.

### What changes

- `--num_serve_frontends` (serve subcommand) default `1 → 8` (`DEFAULT_NUM_SERVE_FRONTENDS` in `commands/serve.py`).
- The **`LlmArgs.num_serve_frontends` field default stays 1**. A bare `LLM()` has no HTTP frontends to fan out to and only `trtllm-serve` can spawn them; keeping the field at 1 means `trtllm-bench`, `trtllm-eval` and Python `LLM()` users do not pay for 8 result lanes / the multi-frontend IPC topology. Because `8 != 1`, the CLI value survives `get_llm_args`'s default filter and reaches the executor; `num_serve_frontends: 1` in the `--config` YAML still overrides it (YAML wins over an untyped CLI default).
- **Graceful fallback for configurations that cannot run more than one frontend.** When the count comes from the default (flag not typed on the CLI and key absent from the YAML) and the config is single-frontend-only — `--grpc`, `--port 0` / `--report_addr`, `orchestrator_type` (`rpc`/`ray`), `enable_resource_governor` — `trtllm-serve` now logs why and runs 1 frontend instead of failing at startup. An explicit `--num_serve_frontends N>1` with such a config still raises, as before (`_resolve_default_num_serve_frontends`). The `--grpc` guard now checks the resolved value so the fallback applies there too.
- The Responses-store warning tells users how to keep the stateful store (`--num_serve_frontends 1`).
- `tests/unittest/api_stability/references/trtllm_serve_cli.yaml`: `serve.num_serve_frontends.default: 8` (the gate fails on the stock reference with `default drift: code=8 vs yaml=1`, verified).
- Docs: new "Multiple HTTP Frontends" section in `docs/source/commands/trtllm-serve/trtllm-serve.rst` (default, opt-out, fallback rules, per-frontend state caveats).

### Behaviour users must know (limitations inherited from #16523, now on by default)

- **Responses API stateful store** (`store` / `previous_response_id`) is disabled with >1 frontend (per-process in-memory store). Opt out with `--num_serve_frontends 1`.
- **Per-frontend observability.** `/metrics`, `/perf_metrics`, `/health` and `/prometheus/metrics` are answered by whichever frontend accepted the connection. With `return_perf_metrics` on, every frontend runs its own iteration-stats collector loop, so the engine's iteration stats are drained per frontend (each sees ~1/K of them) and both the JSON `/metrics` buffer and the iteration-derived Prometheus series (KV-cache gauges, `trtllm_num_requests_completed_total`, iteration latency) reflect only the answering frontend's share; request-level Prometheus series (`trtllm_request_success_total`, TTFT/E2E histograms) live in per-process registries because `PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR` is created in `OpenAIServer.__init__`, after the children are spawned. A scraper therefore sees one frontend's share per scrape and counters appear to reset between scrapes. Without `return_perf_metrics`, `/metrics` drains the engine queue on demand over RPC and the answering frontend returns everything queued, as today. Cross-frontend aggregation (shared multiproc dir set before spawning + gauge `multiprocess_mode`, or a single collector in the launcher) is follow-up work; `--num_serve_frontends 1` restores today's numbers.
- **Host footprint.** Every extra frontend is a full Python process that imports TensorRT LLM and loads the tokenizer (see measurements below); GPU memory is not affected (attached frontends do not create CUDA contexts).
- Disaggregated MPI workers (`disaggregated_mpi_worker`, `disaggregated` fleets), `mm_embedding_serve` and VisualGen are unaffected (the knob is ignored or absent on those entry points).

### Verification

`pre-commit run` passes on all changed files.

Container `gb300-917ad7b3e9` (1.3.0rc26 + this patch applied to `commands/serve.py`), 1× GB300, Qwen3-0.6B, launched the way this cluster runs production (`srun --mpi=pmix … trtllm-llmapi-launch trtllm-serve …`):

| case | command | LISTEN sockets on the port | "Launched attached serving frontend" lines | requests | healthy after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default | `trtllm-serve <model> --config metrics.yaml` | **8** | 7 | 64/64 | 154 s |
| opt-out | `… --num_serve_frontends 1 --config metrics.yaml` | 1 | 0 | 32/32 | 54 s |
| fallback | `… --config rpc.yaml` (`orchestrator_type: rpc`, no flag) | 1 | 0 | 16/16 | 54 s |
| explicit conflict | `… --num_serve_frontends 8 --config rpc.yaml` | — | — | exit 1, `ValueError: num_serve_frontends > 1 requires the default (classic IPC) executor path` | — |

The fallback case logs `num_serve_frontends defaults to 8, but orchestrator_type='rpc' supports a single serving frontend only; running 1 frontend. Pass --num_serve_frontends explicitly to override.` and its `/prometheus/metrics` counters are complete (16/16) like the opt-out case.

- Introspected in-container: click default = 8, `BaseLlmArgs.model_fields["num_serve_frontends"].default` = 1, `--help` renders the new text.
- `api_stability/test_serve_cli.py` passes with the updated reference and fails on the stock one with `[serve] option --num_serve_frontends field default drift: code=8 vs yaml=1`. The fallback resolver was additionally exercised by a throwaway CPU test (every condition → 1, explicit request → unchanged + ValueError) that is not part of the PR.
- Host RSS per attached frontend ≈ 1.99 GB (launcher ≈ 2.5 GB). Attached frontends hold **no GPU memory**: `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps` lists only the worker (58.7 GiB incl. KV cache) and the launcher (748 MiB) in both cases.
- Metrics with 8 frontends: `GET /metrics` returned `[0,1,0,0,0,0,18,19,0,…]` iteration stats over 16 polls; `GET /prometheus/metrics` showed 5 distinct `trtllm_request_success_total` values (6 / 7 / 8 / 10) across 32 scrapes, versus a constant 32/32 with one frontend — the per-frontend sampling described above.
- Clean shutdown after SIGINT in every case: 0 listeners, 0 `trtllm-serve` processes left.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/api_stability/test_serve_cli.py` (reference updated; gates the default)
- `tests/unittest/executor/test_multi_frontend_routing.py` (unchanged, still pins the cap)
- Container e2e above (default / opt-out / fallback / explicit conflict)

## PR Checklist

- [x] PR title follows `[None][feat] ...`
- [x] api_stability reference updated

## Description

title: [None][perf] defer dynamic NVFP4 scale finalization for fused GELU MLPs
body:
## Description

For dynamic NVFP4 quantization in fused GELU MLPs on Blackwell (SM100/SM103), the global activation scale is unknown when launching the up-projection producer. Previously, this required falling back to unfused execution or writing BF16 activations followed by a standalone requantization pass.

This change extends the fused GELU CuteDSL epilogue to support deferred dynamic scale finalization:

1. **Producer (`dense_blockscaled_gemm_act_fusion.py`)**
   - Emits scale-invariant packed Float4E2M1FN output normalized per 16-element block via `div_full_f32(6.0, gmax)` (PTX `div.full.f32`).
   - Writes raw FP32 block scales (`a / 6.0`) directly to global memory in contiguous row-major `[M, N // 16]` layout.
   - Adds `wrapper_deferred_fp4out` to `Sm100BlockScaledPersistentDenseGemmActFusionKernel`.
2. **Runner and custom op (`cute_dsl_custom_ops.py`, `custom_ops/__init__.py`)**
   - Implements `CuteDSLNVFP4GeluDeferredFP4OutBlackwellRunner`.
   - Registers `trtllm::cute_dsl_nvfp4_dense_gemm_gelu_deferred_fp4out_blackwell` with fake-tensor support preserving dynamic batch/token dimensions.
3. **Scale finalizer (`sfc_finalize.py`)**
   - Adds the shared `trtllm::nvfp4_sfc_finalize` kernel to generate swizzled 128x4 scale factors.
   - Guards division by zero when `max_raw == 0.0`, so all-zero tensors produce finite zero metadata.
4. **Consumer scaling (`linear.py`, `utils.py`)**
   - Carries `reciprocal_scale` (`max_raw / 448.0`) in `Fp4QuantizedTensor`.
   - Derives consumer GEMM alpha as `reciprocal_scale * weight_scale_2`.
   - Adds `is_dynamic_nvfp4_input_eligible`.
5. **Module dispatch (`mlp.py`)**
   - Selects deferred FP4 output when `down_proj` uses dynamic NVFP4 and `M >= 128`.
   - Falls back to fused BF16 output for smaller or unsupported configurations.
   - Supports opt-out through `TRTLLM_ENABLE_NVFP4_DEFERRED_GELU=0`.

## Performance

Measured on 8x NVIDIA B300 SXM6 GPUs at the Wan 2.2 distilled I2V Ulysses-8 per-rank FFN geometry (`M=9450, K=5120, N=13824, O=5120`):

| CUDA-event scope | Parent | Deferred | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Up GEMM + bias + tanh-GELU + dynamic NVFP4 production | 0.613856 ms | 0.332224 ms | **1.889131x** |
| Same scope plus shared NVFP4 FC2 | 0.865312 ms | 0.578688 ms | **1.507831x** |

In a same-source Wan 2.2 distilled I2V full-model run (81x720x1280, 8 denoising steps), wall time improved from `5.526483 s` to `5.472929 s` (`1.009785x`), and denoise time improved from `4.306233 s` to `4.242023 s` (`1.015137x`).

## Test Coverage

Added coverage in `tests/unittest/_torch/thop/parallel/test_dense_gemm_act_fusion.py` for:

- Deferred FP4 output and raw-scale finalization against a dynamic reference.
- Bias/no-bias and representative exact/padded shapes.
- The `M >= 128` dispatch threshold and BF16 fallback.
- Consumer alpha derivation from `reciprocal_scale`.
- Finite all-zero scale metadata.
- Fake-tensor shape and dtype registration.

Copy-branch validation:

- `python3 -m py_compile` passed for all ten changed Python files.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.
- The source commit cherry-picked cleanly onto current upstream `main`.

## Description

TRT-LLM currently uses a large variety of caches (e.g., Flashinfer, DeepGEMM, auto-tuner) that can all be configured via separate environment variables, which is cumbersome for end users. At the same time, leveraging warmed-up caches is a good way to speed up TRT-LLM startup and avoid re-compilation of JIT artifacts.

This PR simplifies the above by introducing a `TRTLLM_CACHE_DIR` environment variable which, when set, sets a single root cache directory, under which all known framework caches will be contained. At the moment `TRTLLM_CACHE_DIR` controls the following:

- `TLLM_AUTOTUNER_CACHE_PATH`
- `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR`
- `TRITON_CACHE_DIR`
- `TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR`
- `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE`
- `CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR`
- `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR`
- `TRTLLM_DG_CACHE_DIR`
- `CUDA_CACHE_PATH`

If any of these variables is explicitly set alongside `TRTLLM_CACHE_DIR`, then the framework-specific environment variables will take precedence. Also note that the `TRTLLM_DG_JIT_DUMP_CUBIN` environment variable will be set automatically together with `TRTLLM_CACHE_DIR`, in order to enable cubin dumping in DeepGEMM at `TRTLLM_DG_CACHE_DIR`. Additional caches could be added in the future using the same mechanism.

The unified caching implementation does not collide with the per-rank cache isolation mechanism implemented for Flashinfer: generally, isolation will be enabled if neither of `TRTLLM_CACHE_DIR` or `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE` are set.

## Test Coverage

A series of focused tests was added to ensure that cache priorities are respected (e.g., individual framework caches over `TRTLLM_CACHE_DIR`), that Flashinfer isolation works as expected, and that the proper environment variables are passed from the main process to the MPI workers.

title: [None][perf] Prefix-tokenization cache for MiniMax-M3 (cherry-pick #18389 + M3 hook)

## Description
We find that tokenization becomes bottle for TTFT in high throughput settings in AgentX, as AgentX workload is long sequence. This PR brings the prefix-tokenization cache to the MiniMax-M3 side branch, so that for the multi-turn conversation we don't need to re-tokenize the whole conversation, but we only need to tokenize the tail. 

This PR contains two commits:
1. **cherry-pick of #18389** from @Tabrizian. It adds supports for prefix-tokenization cache. 
2. **MiniMax-M3 code wiring (45 lines in `modeling_minimaxm3_vl.py`)**.

### How to use

```bash
export TLLM_PREFIX_TOKEN_CACHE=1            # opt in (server process)
export TLLM_PREFIX_TOKEN_CACHE_MAX_CHARS=268435456   # optional; AgentX-class prompts fill the 64M default at 25 lanes
trtllm-serve ...                            # log: "Prefix token cache enabled for MiniMax-M3 ..." then hit-rate lines every 1000 requests
```

## Description

On the OpenAI wire an unset optional field is omitted (the official SDK serializes with `exclude_unset`), so an explicit `null` carries no information. But several real clients — litellm among them — serialize every unset optional as `null` when echoing the server's own output items back as multi-turn input: `"logprobs": null` on `output_text` parts, `"caller"`/`"namespace"`/`"status"` null on `function_call` items. The vendored Responses item types validate `null` differently from omitted (`ResponseOutputTextParam.logprobs`: "Input should be iterable"), so a single filled-in null failed the whole request with a 400 on every turn after the first.

This PR fixes it in the request model, mirroring standard OpenAI behavior:

- input items are recursively scrubbed of null-valued keys before the existing per-item shaping in `_drop_unsupported_input_item_keys`;
- null top-level optionals (`tool_choice`, `metadata`, `service_tier`, ...) are dropped so the fields take their defaults; a null required field (`model`, `input`) now reports as missing, which is the accurate contract.

## Test Coverage

title: [TRTLLM-16564][feat] MLA-backboned standalone DSpark drafter (Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark)
body:
## Description

Adds the MLA-backboned standalone DSpark drafter for Kimi-K3, alongside the GQA one already on main.

The GQA drafter stores 16 KV heads x 64, K and V both. Under attention-DP nothing shards it, so every rank holds **20480 B per token**. The MLA drafter holds one 576-wide latent per token per layer: **5760 B**, a 3.6x reduction that does not depend on the parallelism.

Measured on the GEN worker of a DEP16 disaggregated run — two arms whose generated `gen_config.yaml` differ by exactly one line (`speculative_model`), same tree, same MoE backend, same `free_gpu_memory_fraction=0.8`:

| per rank | GQA drafter | MLA drafter | |
|---|---|---|---|
| **KV capacity** | 1,779,275 tok | **2,491,831 tok** | **+40.0%** |
| bytes/token, total | 48,128 | **33,408** | -30.6% |
| bytes/token, target | 27,648 | 27,648 | unchanged |
| bytes/token, draft | 20,480 | **5,760** | -71.9% |
| draft pool | 33.94 GiB | **13.37 GiB** | -20.57 GiB |

Those are the KV manager's own `max_tokens ... New quota is <G>GiB` lines, not derived. Three independent cross-checks agree: draft quota / max_tokens is exactly 5760.0 and 20480.0; solving `target = a*tokens + b` across the two arms gives `a = 27648.0` B/token, identical for both as it must be; and the pool shapes are `5 x (194785, 1, 1, 64, 576)` bf16 for MLA against `5 x (139005, 2, 16, 64, 64)` for GQA. The residual `b = 7.53 GiB` is the token-independent KDA per-sequence state, which is why capacity rises 40.0% rather than the 44.1% the bytes/token ratio alone would suggest.

`MLADSparkForCausalLM` is selected from the checkpoint's own `architectures`, so switching drafters is one line of config. It brings its own absorbed-MLA block decode rather than borrowing the worker's attention backend (`_uses_worker_attention_backend = False`), and takes its context KV from the draft KV cache manager's pool rather than a `max_seq_len`-dense private arena (`_paged_ctx_cache = True`) — the arena needs 78.5 GiB at 1M context, which is what made the MLA drafter undeployable before #18343 landed.

### One user-visible default moves

`DSparkDecodingConfig.attention_backend` goes `VANILLA` -> `AUTO`, and `AUTO` resolves per drafter family: an MLA backbone to its absorbed-MLA paged decode, a GQA backbone to the trtllm-gen op set, degrading to `VANILLA` when those ops are unavailable. A standalone GQA DSpark deployment that did not set the field therefore moves from FlashAttention to trtllm-gen. Nothing raises that did not raise before on that family — only the MLA one refuses to degrade, because a build that cannot run its kernel cannot hold the target either. The `Literal` only gains values (`AUTO`, `CUTEDSL`), so existing configs stay valid; `tests/unittest/api_stability` reference files are unchanged, since they record `speculative_config`'s union type rather than each config's fields.

### Block reuse

`kv_cache_config.enable_block_reuse: true` costs the drafter acceptance: the target skips a cached prefix, the drafter's context does not follow, so it cross-attends over the newly computed tail alone. Lossless — the target verifies every token — so AL is the only symptom. [NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#18093](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/18093) built the one-model draft KV reuse protocol but its scope table excludes DFlash/DSpark; these two commits join them to it, and `_store_prefill_context` indexes the tail from the absolute position instead of overwriting the prefix from 0.

Teacher-forced multi-turn, T=0, C=1, every `(conversation, turn)` prompt byte-identical across arms. 20 trajectories, 522 paired turns, SE clustered on conversation [measured job 3084626, on the source branch]:

| subset | reuse ON before | **after** | reuse OFF | SGLang | turns |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| workflow | 1.7778 | **2.2343** | 2.2018 | 2.2610 | 151 |
| coding | 2.4603 | **3.3932** | 3.2861 | 3.3834 | 371 |
| **ALL** | 2.2056 | **2.9450** | 2.8714 | 2.9482 | 522 |

`SGLang − this branch` is `+0.0231` (SE 0.0335, t = 0.69), i.e. indistinguishable.

### Why this is not split further

The drafter, the KV-budget fix and the backend selection are one deployable unit: the drafter cannot run without the per-request page bound (it corrupts a neighbour's pages), and it cannot be *budgeted* without charging the draft pool at its allocated dtype (the split hands it half the target's tokens and the GEN worker dies at ~50% target utilization, fatal to every rank). Landing any one alone leaves a configuration that loads and then fails in production. The commits are separable for review and each carries its own test.

## Test Coverage

All numbers below are from this branch rebased onto current `main` (236 upstream commits, four files conflict-resolved), in the container the editable env was built against.

**Unit — 13 suites, 236 passed / 4 skipped / 0 failed**, plus `test_kda_mtp_decode_cute_parity.py` 30 passed. The 41 tests this PR adds break down as:

- *Falsifiable against a named commit* (14): each asserts a value the pre-fix code cannot produce — e.g. `test_inherited_fp8_kv_algo_is_dropped_from_the_draft_cost` asserts `cost.slope == 5760`, which is `2880` without the fix; `test_mla_block_fixup_stays_inside_the_allocation` asserts every page is `42` with a negative control that lands on page `0`; `test_prepare_keeps_cuda_graph_slots_across_replays` reads `[7,8,9]` across two `prepare()` calls where the old path reset to `[0,0,0]`.
- *Numeric parity with a negative control* (5): absorbed vs un-absorbed MLA, SWA vs full attention, adjacent-pair vs HF RoPE. Each pairs a tolerance with a control that must be far outside it (K/V halves swapped lands 89-201x away), so a degenerate output cannot pass.
- *Construction-time contract* (19): the backend policy and weight-loading guards. These cannot run on `main` at all — the class does not exist there — so their answer to "red on which commit" is "absent before the feature commit". Three match on exact error strings.

**Disaggregated GSM8K**, TEP16 1xCTX + 1xGEN, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, against the same config before the rebase:

| | pre-rebase | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| strict-match | 0.9629 | **0.9666** ±0.0049 |
| drafter AL | 3.713 | **3.715** |
| drafter AR | 38.8% | **38.8%** |
| `not aligned to 16 bytes` in CTX | 16 ranks | **0** |

AL is `1 + sum(i*hist[i]) / sum(hist)` over all 16 ranks' `dflash_accept_stats_rank*.json` — the denominator is request-steps, not `num_steps`, which counts iterations and would overstate AL ~7.7x. The GEN worker logs `DFlash: ctx block tables` 32 times, so this exercises the managed paged pool rather than the private arena; the arena fallback would make the run vacuous.

**Aggregated GSM8K + acceptance**, TEP16, n=200, 0-shot (the drafter was distilled on chat traffic), against two pre-rebase runs of the same arm:

| | pre-rebase A | pre-rebase B | this branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| AL | 5.505 | 5.390 | **5.534** |
| AR | 66.3% | 64.6% | **66.7%** |
| flexible-extract | 84 | 86.5 | **83** ±2.7 |

The two pre-rebase runs differ from each other by 0.115 AL and 1.7pt AR, so this run sits inside the arm's own spread. `strict-match` is 0 in all three: at 0-shot the model never sees the `#### <answer>` form, so the strict filter matches nothing by construction.

Two gaps worth stating rather than hiding:

- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_budget_split.py` is in no CI test list, so the three tests added there do not run in CI. The gap pre-dates this PR (`l0_cpu.yml` covers `unittest/_torch/speculative/hw_agnostic` as a directory, but `_torch/executor/kv_cache` is listed file-by-file).
- The reuse extension's own guard (`first_pos + slen > covered` -> `RuntimeError`) is subsumed here by this branch's per-request `cap`, which is the same quantity (`_ctx_block_counts[i] * page_size`) and skips the request with a warning rather than killing the forward for every other in-flight request.
- The flashinfer MLA decode call's `lse=` / `return_lse=` keyword pair is exercised only through the parity test, not asserted directly.

## Review follow-ups

Landed after the first review round:

- **The paged generation path raised `AttributeError`.** Upstream's merged #18343 bounds the drafter's context writes by the block-table width and defines no `_ctx_block_counts`; the branch this was developed on defines it, so the port carried the consumer without its producer. Restored, and both write paths — generation and `_store_prefill_context` — are now bounded by the same quantity rather than only the advertised read length.
- **That bound is per-request on one backend only.** `copyBatchBlockOffsetsToDeviceKernel` maps `BAD_PAGE_INDEX` to `0` (`kvCacheManagerV2Utils.cu:231`) and `TLLM_KV_CACHE_MANAGER_V2_BACKEND` defaults to `cpp`, so there the count saturates at the table width and the bound degenerates to exactly what upstream already applied. It is real on the `python` backend, which propagates the sentinel. Stated in `dflash_allocated_ctx_limit`'s docstring so nobody reads a guarantee into it.
- The draft-KV dtype carve-out is narrowed from `is_external_drafter()` to `is_dflash() or is_dspark()`, matching `_should_create_separate_draft_kv_cache`; PARD and DRAFT_TARGET_ONE_MODEL reach that helper too and can carry a genuine fp8 KV algo of their own.
- `_runtime_position_ceiling` is declared on `DFlashForCausalLM` instead of injected, the MLA RoPE table is keyed on its resolved cap so a re-published ceiling rebuilds it, a guard whose named failure mode now raises one frame down was removed, and a `try/except` around a diagnostic that cannot fail was dropped.
- Tests: the allocation-bound test calls the production clamp instead of restating it and gains a negative control at the regression boundary; two parameterized tests drive both `KIMI_K3_AUX_ATTN_RES_STREAM` conventions through the real layer forward and the model tail.

## Also in this branch

Two ancillary commits that touch the same files and are not part of the feature:

- A comment correction in the draft-mirror saturation path. Skipping a context request whose mirror found no IndexMapper slot does not defer it to the next iteration — `copy_batch_block_offsets` runs later in the same iteration and `IndexMapper::getCopyIndex` feeds every id in the batch, context ids included, to `getIndex()`, which `TLLM_CHECK`s on an unmapped id. Behaviour is unchanged and predates the mirror refactor; only the claim about it was wrong.
- `_get_draft_kv_model_config()`, so the KV budget split charges the external drafter at the dtype its pool is actually allocated at. `kv_cache_config.dtype: fp8` stamps the target's algo onto every loaded model; the allocation path stripped it back off for an external drafter but the cost path did not, charging 2880 B/token for a pool costing 5760.

## PR Checklist

- PR description clearly explains what and why — yes, including the one default-value change above.
- PR follows [TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of my knowledge.
- Test cases are provided for new code paths — yes, 41 new tests, classified above.
- API changes: the `attention_backend` `Literal` only gains values and `tests/unittest/api_stability` references are unchanged, so this is **`api-compatible`**, not breaking. `tensorrt_llm/usage/llm_args_golden_manifest.json` is regenerated and committed, as `AGENTS.md` requires.
- New dependencies: none.
- CODEOWNERS: unchanged. The manifest edit pulls in `trt-llm-usage-telemetry-devs`, `trt-llm-oss-compliance` and `trt-llm-noncommitted-api-review-committee` per `.github/CODEOWNERS:496`.
- Documentation: no user-facing doc change; the new architecture name `K3DsparkForCausalLM` is deliberately **not** added to `tensorrt_llm/usage/architecture_allowlist.py`, since the checkpoint is not publicly documented by TensorRT-LLM. Telemetry hashes it, which fails closed.
- tava architecture diagram: no change, this adds a drafter behind existing interfaces.

- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

title: [#19240][fix] Do not dereference an empty tactic list
body:
Fixes #19240.

### Problem

`selectTacticsForArch` has a fallback for "no tactic matched the filters"
(`cpp/tests/unit_tests/kernels/mixtureOfExpertsTest.cu:1295-1303`):

```cpp
if (it1 == tactics1.end() || it2 == tactics2.end())
{
    // Fall back to any tactic
    std::cout << "WARNING: Could not find config for sm version " << sm << std::endl;
    it1 = (it1 == tactics1.end()) ? tactics1.begin() : it1;
    it2 = (it2 == tactics2.end()) ? tactics2.begin() : it2;
}

return std::pair(*it1, *it2);
```

It does not cover the case where the list is empty. There `begin() == end()`, so the
dereference below is undefined.

### Change

Four lines: check for an empty list before the fallback and report it with both sizes.

### Verification

Container `nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/devel:1.3.0rc26`, commit `63d217f2`, NVIDIA B300
SXM6 (compute capability 10.3), built with:

```bash
python3 scripts/build_wheel.py --skip_building_wheel --skip-stubs \
  --cuda_architectures 103-real --build_type RelWithDebInfo --fast_build \
  -D "SANITIZE=address" -D "BUILD_TESTS=ON"
```

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `make mixtureOfExpertsTest` | builds | builds, 0 errors |
| `MixtureOfExpertsTest/5.Permute` | `AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address 0x40` | `No MoE GEMM tactics available for sm 103 (GEMM_1: 0, GEMM_2: 0)` |
| SEGV count in the run | 1 | 0 |

The reported sizes confirm the list was empty rather than merely unmatched, which is what
separates this path from the one the existing fallback was written for.

The test still fails, because the parameter set genuinely has no tactic on this device.
Turning that into a skip rather than a failure is a separate decision, so this change only
removes the undefined behaviour and makes the reason visible.

### What I did not check

- Whether the same parameter set has tactics on other architectures.
- Whether `getTactics` returning an empty list here is itself expected. That question is in
  #19240 and is for maintainers to answer.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Dev Engineer Review

`selectTacticsForArch` now checks for empty GEMM tactic lists before fallback dereferencing. It reports the SM version and tactic counts instead of invoking undefined behavior. The change is localized and does not alter public APIs.

## QA Engineer Review

No test changes.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `cpp/tests/unit_tests/kernels/mixtureOfExpertsTest.cu`: Verify the empty-list diagnostic and existing fallback behavior for non-empty lists. Test-list coverage was not changed; the affected test still fails when no tactic exists.

title: [#19193][fix] Locate Torch when BUILD_PYT is off
body:
Fixes #19193.

### Problem

`--cpp_only` (documented in `docs/source/installation/build-from-source.md:87` as "Build
only the C++ runtime library, without Python bindings") cannot configure on `main`:

```
CMake Error at tensorrt_llm/runtime/utils/CMakeLists.txt:28 (find_library):
  Could not find TORCH_PYTHON_LIB using the following names: torch_python

-- Configuring incomplete, errors occurred!
```

Torch discovery lives inside `if(BUILD_PYT)` at `cpp/CMakeLists.txt:529`, so with
`BUILD_PYT=OFF` neither `TORCH_INSTALL_PREFIX` nor `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` is populated, and
three unguarded call sites fail: `runtime/utils/CMakeLists.txt:28`,
`executor/cache_transmission/ucx_utils/CMakeLists.txt:6`, and
`batch_manager/CMakeLists.txt:105`.

Supplying the paths by hand is not enough, because core C++ headers include torch
unconditionally:

```
include/tensorrt_llm/batch_manager/cacheTransceiver.h:28
  -> include/tensorrt_llm/runtime/utils/pgUtils.h:24
    -> torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/ProcessGroup.hpp, torch/torch.h
tensorrt_llm/common/ncclUtils.h:25 -> ATen/cuda/CUDAContext.h
tensorrt_llm/kernels/trtllmGenKernels/blockScaleMoe/runner.h
  -> tensorrt_llm/thop/thUtils.h:22 -> ATen/cuda/CUDAContext.h
```

### Change

Run the Torch discovery regardless of `BUILD_PYT`, and keep only
`add_compile_definitions(TORCH_CUDA=1)` conditional. The `else()` branch that set
`-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=0` for a torch-less build is unreachable once Torch is always
required, so it is removed.

This reflects what the sources already need. It does not attempt the larger question
raised in #19193, namely whether the C++ runtime should depend on torch at all. If you
would rather decouple `cacheTransceiver` from `c10d` and keep `--cpp_only` free of torch,
I am happy to redo this as that change instead.

Most of the diff is re-indentation. `git diff -w` reports 7 insertions and 9 deletions.

### Verification

Inside `nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/devel:1.3.0rc26`, x86_64, CUDA 13.2, PyTorch
2.12.0a0+5aff3928d8.nv26.05:

| Command | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `build_wheel.py --cpp_only -a 90-real` | CMake Error at `runtime/utils/CMakeLists.txt:28` | `Build files have been written`, 0 CMake errors |
| `make pg_utils` | not reached | `Built target pg_utils` |
| `make common_src` | not reached | `Built target common_src` |
| `make trtllm_gen_fp8_block_scale_moe_routing` | not reached | `Built target trtllm_gen_fp8_block_scale_moe_routing` |
| `build_wheel.py -a 90-real` (BUILD_PYT=ON) | `Configuring done (85.0s)` | `Configuring done (88.9s)`, 0 CMake errors |

The three targets above are the ones covering the three headers listed earlier.

### What I did not check

- I did not run a `--cpp_only` build to completion, only the three targets that previously
  failed to compile, plus configure.
- I did not check Windows, or any compiler other than the container's GCC.
- I did not run the test suite.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Dev Engineer Review

`cpp/CMakeLists.txt` now discovers Torch when `BUILD_PYT=OFF`, enabling unguarded runtime, UCX, and batch-manager Torch dependencies to configure. `TORCH_CUDA=1` remains Python-only, and the unreachable torch-less ABI branch was removed.

The complete C++-only build, Windows builds, alternate compilers, and test suite were not verified.

## QA Engineer Review

No test changes.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `cpp/CMakeLists.txt`: Verify Torch discovery for Python-enabled and C++-only builds. Confirm correct CUDA and ABI behavior for both configurations.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: [TRTLLM-16466][fix] Profile cached KV chunks for dense MLA
body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- Adds chunk-aware MLA KV-cache profiling for bounded chunked prefill on SM100+.
- Removes the workspace reserve and admission cap only after profiling succeeds.
- Retains protections for unsupported or unprofiled paths, including DSA fallback, SM90 full-gather dispatch, and applicable Hopper configurations.
- Extends `get_mla_context_workspace_kv_len_cap(...)` with profiling controls.
- Review severity counts are unavailable.
- GPU integration, full CPU testing, accuracy investigation, and original-environment revalidation remain pending.

## QA Engineer Review

- Adds 24 parameterized KV-cache estimation tests for chunk sizing, context limits, workspace state, cache limits, hardware gating, and fallback behavior.
- Enables chunked prefill in `TestKimiK2.test_nvfp4`.
- No test-list files changed. Test-list registration is not confirmed.
- Coverage verdict: **needs follow-up**.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/_util.py`: Verify the new profiling controls, chunked-prefill sizing, reserve removal, admission-cap behavior, and fallback paths.
- `tests/integration/defs/accuracy/test_llm_api_pytorch.py`: Verify Kimi K2 NVFP4 accuracy with chunked prefill enabled. Test-list registration is not confirmed.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_estimation.py`: Verify parameterized coverage for hardware, chunking, workspace state, cache limits, MLA modes, and scheduler rounding. Test-list registration is not confirmed.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Addresses [TRTLLM-16466](https://jirasw.nvidia.com/browse/TRTLLM-16466).

Fresh-prompt KV-cache profiling does not exercise the cached-KV staging buffers used by dense MLA with prefix reuse. Enable chunked prefill in `TestKimiK2::test_nvfp4` and profile real cached prefixes before sizing the KV pool from the allocation peak.

For dense TRTLLM MLA on the SM100+ cached-KV chunk path, the profiler submits a long request per attention-DP rank. With KV chunk capacity C and query budget Q, its length is ceil(2*C/Q)*Q + Q. This exercises two full cached-KV chunks in one forward with a full query, including the overlap while tensors from the previous chunk remain live during the next expansion. With max_num_tokens=8192 and C=32768, the request has 73728 tokens and reaches 65536 cached + 8192 new tokens. Temporary KV capacity is calculated from these requests using the existing estimator. Configurations whose context limit cannot fit this request retain the applicable reserve/cap protection. GPU peak-memory comparison of this revised length remains pending.

After this profiling run completes, skip the old additional workspace reserve and attended-KV admission cap for the covered path. Preserve the C++ workspace-sizing fix. Beam search, speculative decoding, and skip-softmax use the same dense context path and are eligible; existing temporary-cache sizing already accounts for beam width and speculative token extras. Existing runtime compatibility checks still apply.

On SM100+, unprofiled chunked paths retain reserve/cap protection where the backend declares a nonzero workspace cost. DSA dense fallback cannot be covered generically by one long prompt because it may switch to sparse before reaching a full chunk. Hopper preserves its pre-PR backend-declared reserve/cap policy: dense MLA with scheduler chunking enabled does not gain a new reservation or admission cap. SM90 remains excluded from chunk-aware profiling because its cached-KV path still uses full-gather. Existing reservations for non-chunked reuse and backend-declared unbounded workspace remain unchanged on Hopper; addressing its full-gather memory risk is outside this PR. This PR does not globally delete the remaining protection.

## Test Coverage

- Added 24 parameterized cases in `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_estimation.py`: ADP/non-ADP request construction, context-length limits, runtime chunk dimensions, reserve gating, beam/spec/skip-softmax eligibility, hardware dispatch, and unsupported-path fallback. The existing `l0_cpu` executor-directory entry includes this file.
- Executed those cases against the changed source methods in a release container using real torch and executor request bindings: 24 passed. Methods were isolated from unrelated current-main imports; this is not a full repository pytest run. A direct current-source test-file attempt was blocked at collection because the rc25 KV-cache-manager-v2 binding lacks the `poison_reason` API required by current Python source.
- Repository pre-commit checks and `git diff --check`.
- Additional one-B300 compatibility matrix using small DeepSeek-shaped models, query budget 128, KV chunk 512, and profiling prompt 672. Dense, beam=2, MTP (both variants), NGram, SA, EAGLE3, draft-target, and skip-softmax all completed initialization and generation while exercising both full and multiple cached-KV chunks during profiling.
- DSA with/without dense fallback, short contexts, disabled chunking, and FlashInfer BF16 also completed execution. These successes do not all prove the dense-chunk profiling bound: with a DSA fallback threshold of 384, profiling reached only 256 cached tokens in dense mode before switching to absorption, but the reuse workload later reached **768 cached + 120 new** in dense mode. Keep its protection.
- Two matrix configurations failed for image/backend reasons: FlashInfer FP8 on SM103 rejects the selected fa2 MLA backend, and the old image's VANILLA MLA rejects its metadata type. These are not claims about every current-main configuration of those backends.

The compatibility matrix used the rc24 runtime with the changed request-construction methods transplanted and eligibility exclusions temporarily removed to inspect each path. EAGLE3 used explicit capture layers and non-Lite Q-LoRA. Draft-target used a dense-FFN draft with normal loading from small random-weight HF checkpoints (the existing dummy loader assumes a draft weight-sharing method), plus current-main's existing optional engine weight-loader guard. This is execution/coverage evidence, not a full current-main integration or accuracy run. GPU scripts and detailed logs are retained in the experiment workspace.

- Prior prototype experiment on 4xB300, Kimi-K2-Thinking-NVFP4, TP4 + attention DP, FP8 KV, `max_num_tokens=8192`, `max_batch_size=16`, KV fraction 0.8:

| Variant | Allocated KV pool / GPU | MMLU | GSM8K |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Existing reserve/cap | 49.93 GiB | 88.47% | 94.12% |
| Reserve/cap removed | 79.04 GiB | 88.47% | 93.52% |
| Chunking + chunk-aware profiling | 76.90 GiB | 88.23% | 93.40% |

The prototype recovered approximately **26.97 GiB of KV pool capacity per GPU** (107.88 GiB across four GPUs); rank-0 profiling peak increased by 2.68 GiB. All runs completed without OOM. Full-chunk and multi-chunk coverage was observed on all ranks. These measurements are from the earlier rc24 prototype, not an end-to-end run of this PR's current-main commit.

## Draft follow-up

- Run the updated Kimi-K2 integration test and full CPU tests on the final source revision.
- Investigate score/output differences before claiming no accuracy regression.
- Revalidate on the original OOM environment; the larger-memory B300 experiment did not reproduce the original OOM.
- Extend profiling coverage before removing the remaining reserve/cap infrastructure globally.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Scope, implementation, validation, and known limitations are described above.
- [x] Regression tests are included in an existing CPU CI test directory.
- [x] No public API or dependency changes.
- Final-source GPU integration and accuracy validation remain pending; see Draft follow-up above.

- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

title: [None][refactor] modularize Mamba cache managers
body:
## Summary

The Mamba cache manager previously combined shared pool lifecycle code with model-specific replay and auxiliary state. This refactor separates the V2 lifecycle, shared contracts, and legacy implementations, and moves model behavior into the Mamba2, GDN, KDA, and Qwen4 module directories.

- Each model returns a validated `MambaState` from `_initialize_model_state()`. The V2 base delegates intermediate-buffer access, binding, reset, accepted-state updates, layer payloads, replay metadata, and shutdown through that interface.
- Missing intermediate buffers are represented by `None` in the state implementation. The base does not inspect concrete replay types.
- The Mamba2 seed accessor stays in Nemotron/Mamba2 and legacy implementations, including non-MTP stochastic rounding. Qwen4 PLE/QSA and KDA relocation/transfer hooks remain model-specific.
- Registered persistent-buffer roles define warmup cleanup; replay/intermediate scratch, indices, and seeds retain their existing lifecycle. The unrelated K3 MegaMoE compatibility change has been reverted; K3 validation uses CUTLASS.

## Testing

- NVIDIA B300: **306 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, process exit code 0, across `test_mamba_model_managers.py`, `test_mamba_cache_manager.py`, and `test_mamba_ssm_rand_seed.py`.
- Coverage includes the state contract, absent-buffer semantics, model factory/lifecycle behavior, PLE buffers, KDA relocation/transfer, non-MTP seed reset, and preservation of scratch during warmup cleanup.
- Normal pre-commit hooks and DCO sign-off passed.
- Full speculative accuracy validation remains in progress. Earlier integration results predate the latest interface change and are not claimed as end-to-end validation of this commit.

[Architecture and interface documentation](https://mamba-hybrid-manager-architecture.lfy.nvidia.com/) (NVIDIA internal).

The validation above supersedes the earlier validation status in the generated review below.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

The PR modularizes Mamba cache management into shared, legacy, and model-specific V2 modules. It adds model-owned state handling for Mamba2, GDN, KDA, and Qwen4-Exp PLE/QSA.

Routing, replay selection, state-transfer completion, V1 deprecation warnings, and cache-parameter ownership changed. Verify manager selection, replay compatibility, disaggregated transfers, cache sizing, lazy exports, and legacy imports. Full speculative accuracy validation remains in progress.

## QA Engineer Review

The PR modifies unit and integration tests for cache-manager contracts, lifecycle behavior, replay metadata, KDA/GDN behavior, Qwen4-Exp PLE, QSA wiring, Mamba metadata, and Nemotron speculative configuration. Coverage includes layout validation, slot relocation, acceptance tracking, dummy requests, state transfer, buffer accounting, and compatibility behavior.

title: [#19485][fix] Clamp top-p searchsorted index to prevent OOB scatter when cumulative probability stays below top_p
body:
## Description

When `top_p` is very close to 1.0 (e.g. `0.9999999`), FP32 cumulative probability accumulation can fail to reach `top_p` for some rows. `torch.searchsorted()` then returns `vocab_size` (out-of-bounds), causing a CUDA device-side assert on GPU or `IndexError` on CPU when used as a scatter/gather index.

### Root Cause

In [`top_k_top_p_sampling_batch`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/sampler/ops/vanilla.py), the code assumes every row of `cumulative_probs` will contain at least one element `>= top_p`. When this assumption is violated by finite-precision accumulation, `torch.searchsorted` returns `vocab_size` — an index one past the last valid column — which is then passed directly to `scatter_` and used as a gather index for renormalization.

### Fix

Clamp `last_index_to_keep` to `vocab_size - 1`. When clamped, the mask entry at the last position is already `False`, so the scatter is a no-op, all tokens are retained, and renormalization uses the actual cumulative sum. This is the correct behavior: if the cumulative sum cannot reach `top_p`, no tokens should be filtered out.

Fixes: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/issues/19485

## Description

Enables the `MEGAMOE_CUTEDSL` MoE backend for the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4
checkpoint.

The 48 routed expert layers of that checkpoint already clear every
`MegaMoECuteDsl` gate on SM100 — NVFP4, bfloat16 activations, plain SwiGLU,
`hidden_size` 2560 (divisible by 32), `moe_intermediate_size` 640 (divisible
by 16), top-k 10 — so `moe_config.backend: MEGAMOE_CUTEDSL` runs them on the
fused dispatch / FC1 / activation / FC2 / combine kernel. The backend is
expert-parallel only (`moe_tensor_parallel_size: 1`), and under attention DP
it requires `moe_expert_parallel_size == tensor_parallel_size`.

MTP is not part of this configuration. The checkpoint keeps the MTP layer's
experts at block-scaled FP8, which `MegaMoECuteDsl` does not serve (NVFP4
only) and which `CutlassFusedMoE` does not serve on SM100 either, so the MTP
layer has no eligible implementation. This mirrors the existing `CUTEDSL`
coverage for the same checkpoint.

The one production change is in `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock`: a `MEGAMOE_*`
request now passes `allow_backend_degradation=False`. Previously a declined
MegaMoE request fell back to CUTLASS silently, so a run would be measured as
if it were MegaMoE and the new test would cover nothing. The resolver now
raises with its rejection trail instead. `KimiK3MoERuntime` already does this
for the same reason. A layer whose experts are excluded from quantization is
unaffected: that path rewrites the backend to CUTLASS first, so degradation
stays allowed there.

## Description

`build_wheel.py` runs the cmake configure step only on `--clean`, first build, or explicit `--configure_cmake`. Passing a configuration-affecting flag (e.g. `--nvrtc_dynamic_linking`, a changed `--cuda_architectures`, or `--extra-cmake-vars`) against an existing build dir therefore silently builds the previous configuration. Concrete failure: a build dir configured without `--nvrtc_dynamic_linking` keeps linking `CUDA::nvrtc_static` after the flag is added, which fails at link on CUDA 13.4 toolkits that no longer ship the static library — after a full compile cycle.

This change fingerprints the resolved configure arguments (sha256 over the sorted cmake definitions plus build type, targets, CUDA architectures, generator, and python executable) into `<build_dir>/.cmake_configure_args.sha256` at configure time. On subsequent runs, a differing fingerprint forces reconfigure and prints one line explaining why. Build dirs predating the fingerprint file keep the current behavior until their next configure.

`--configure_cmake` remains as the explicit override; no new flags.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/others/test_build_wheel_reconfigure.py` (new): fingerprint order-independence, content sensitivity, digest form, and stored-fingerprint round-trip/missing/empty handling.
- `python3 -m py_compile scripts/build_wheel.py` and pre-commit clean.

CI merge pipelines failed, but no failure cause was provided.

title: [TRTLLM-16593][fix] Size expanded draft probabilities by batch capacity
body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

Fixes [TRTLLM-16593](https://jirasw.nvidia.com/browse/TRTLLM-16593).

When one-model rejection sampling requires expansion from the draft vocabulary to the target vocabulary, `full_draft_probs` is allocated with `num_slot_rows` (the request-slot capacity plus a dummy row). However, this tensor is scratch space for the generation batch after gathering slot-indexed draft probabilities, so its first dimension only needs `max_num_requests`.

Allocate `full_draft_probs` with shape `[max_num_requests, max_draft_len, vocab_size]`. Preserve the allocation guard, zero initialization, slot-indexed `draft_probs`, its dummy row, and shared buffer reuse by CUDA graph metadata. This reduces FP32 storage by `(num_slot_rows - max_num_requests) * max_draft_len * vocab_size * 4` bytes.

## Test Coverage

- No new test cases. Update the existing vocabulary-mismatch test shape assertion from `(R + 1, K, V)` to `(R, K, V)` to reflect the corrected batch capacity.
- Prior GPU validation passed **34 tests** using the buffer-guard suite (including temporary regression checks) and `tests/unittest/_torch/speculative/hw_agnostic/test_advanced_sampling_mode.py`. The additional regression checks were used during validation and are not included in this PR. The existing guard test file is already included in the H100 L0 configuration.
- H200 model validation: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (target vocabulary 128,256) with EAGLE3-LLaMA3.1-Instruct-8B (draft vocabulary 32,000), TP=1, BF16, batch capacity 8, draft length 4. Tested 16 MTBench prompts in batches of 1/3/8/4, with temperature 1 and fixed seeds, in both eager and CUDA graph modes.
  - All **2,048 output tokens** matched baseline exactly across the two modes. The eager rejection trace also matched across 185 calls; each graph run performed 141 actual graph replays.
  - Buffer storage decreased from **18,468,864 to 16,416,768 bytes**. CUDA allocated memory and per-batch peak allocated memory decreased by **2 MiB** in both modes.
- Separate synthetic GPU operator tests checked gathered/expanded probabilities and rejection-sampler outputs, including high slot indices and the dummy slot. With batch/slot capacities 64/128, draft length 4, and vocabulary 128,256, tensor storage savings were **127.21 MiB**; with 128/256, draft length 8, and vocabulary 151,936, savings were **598.14 MiB**. These are synthetic configurations, not the measured model-run savings above.

title: [https://nvbugs/6759021][test] Re-enable disagg single-GPU tests for the MPI orchestrator
body:
## Description

The DLFW 26.08 upgrade (#18126) skipped the whole `test_disaggregated_single_gpu.py` module and waived seven cases under https://nvbugs/6759021 because the Ray stage hung on the Open MPI 5 shipped by the new base image.

Investigation on H100 with the 26.08 image shows the hang is **specific to the Ray orchestrator**: workers spawned through MPI never return from `ray.init()`, because the raylet forked from an MPI-spawned process does not answer its clients' `RegisterClient` requests (confirmed with py-spy native stacks and a 25-line reproducer that does not involve TensorRT-LLM). The MPI orchestrator path passes, so the module-wide skip was dropping healthy coverage on the MPI stages (l0_h100 pre-merge, l0_a10).

This PR restores the MPI-side coverage while keeping the Ray stage tracked:

- Narrow the module-level skip to the Ray orchestrator only (`TLLM_DISABLE_MPI=1`), referencing https://nvbugs/6759021.
- Add a module-scoped autouse fixture that performs one trivial MPI spawn before the tests run. On Open MPI 5, `MPI.Publish_name` fails with `MPI_ERR_INTERN` in a singleton-initialized process unless a PRRTE DVM is already running; the first dynamic spawn bootstraps that DVM for the process lifetime. Without this, the tests only passed when an earlier test in the same pytest session happened to spawn MPI workers (https://nvbugs/6770878).
- Remove the seven nvbugs/6759021 waives.

## Test Coverage

Verified on H100 with the 26.08 image (self-built wheel from current main):
